- **Pause/Play and tab-visibility reopens in the Partition Viewer and Log Viewer now resume from the current live offset, not a stale Replay seek.** After Replay (or picking an older segment) catches up to the live tail, the catch-up flip is a display-only signal (`SeekTracker`) that never told the shared `useGatedSubscription` gate the seek was done — so the ORIGINAL replay-start position stayed recorded forever, and the next Pause→Play or tab hide→refocus jumped back to it instead of continuing from the most-recently-displayed message. An explicit seek is now single-use: the moment it's delivered, the recorded target reverts to "resume live" (`resumePositions()`), so only the one delivery it was meant for uses it.
- **`invalidate_options_cache()` now purges each schema key's own option-cache entry, not just the two aggregate groups.** It previously only busted WordPress's `alloptions`/`notoptions` caches; WP core also caches every option under its own key, so a long-running process (a supervisor `tick_loop()`) that had already read a specific option once could keep serving that stale value indefinitely even though `reset()` runs every 15s. The purge now loops `Settings_Schema::get()->overlay_keys()` alongside the aggregate deletes.
- **The Probe button's roll-up never rendered even after the dispatch fix.** The card read `fleet.probes?.[server.id]`, but the fleet view stores each result keyed by whatever id `onProbe` was called with — `server.vault_id`, per the fix above. Same class of mismatch, second occurrence; both render-path tests had fixtures keyed to match the wrong lookup, so neither caught it.
- **The Aggregator tab's per-spoke Probe button always failed with "server not found".** It passed the topology node name (`server.id`, e.g. `firehose:tw0`) to `cmd_probe`, which resolves a Vault *credential key* (`server.vault_id`) — a different identifier whenever the two diverge. The existing test only passed because its fixture happened to make them equal; it now seeds a distinct vault_id so the mismatch can't regress silently.
- **The paused toolbar button's glyph is visible in dark skins.** The shared `.is-paused` state paired the brass background with `var(--ink)` at rest — bright ink on bright brass in CRT-style skins made the ⏸/▶ glyph vanish (its hover state already used `var(--on-accent)`, which the resting state now matches).
- **Tail streams now carry the position breadcrumb, un-breaking the Log Viewer's Replay→Live flip on a live server.** `Tail_Node::forward_line()` minted every line with an empty `Message::ID` — a deliberate pre-seek-era omission whose docblock claimed the offset was unused — so the browser seek tracker never saw the `inode:offset:length` (file) / `segment:offset:length` (segmented) breadcrumbs its catch-up flip reads, and the fail-safe kept Replay lit forever. The integration test passed because its fake injected exactly the ID production omitted; the emit now stamps the Tail's own position (mirroring the base pump's stamp), pinned by real-Tail emit tests in both modes.
- **The debug-overlay console no longer crashes the browser tab when connected to a firehose.** Connecting the overlay console to a viewer's stream `Tee` and clicking an older segment replays that segment (up to 64 MB) at full speed, fanning every record into the `_output` `Dumper`. The Dumper published per message — a `setState('transcript')` that drove a synchronous React re-render AND a `localStorage` transcript write for EACH record — so at thousands of records/sec the main thread fell behind the EventSource event queue and the content process ran out of memory. Per-message work is now O(1) into a bounded ring, and the publish is coalesced to one animation-frame flush; a console flooded past the ring cap drops with a rate-limited count (MemorySieve degrade) instead of OOMing. Interactive command replies still publish immediately (only data-plane frames coalesce).

## [0.48.2] - 2026-07-21

### Fixed

- **Timeline modal: the Trace toggle sits in line with the filter inputs** instead of on its own toolbar row — TimelineView gained an `actions` slot leading the filters row, and the filter pair holds the right edge.

## [0.48.1] - 2026-07-21

### Fixed

- **The all-nodes Trace toggle moved from the Runtime modal to the Timeline modal.** Traces are what populate the timeline — its empty state points at the Trace button — so the toggle now lives beside its output; Runtime is back to pure timers/handles grids. In transit the toggle's reconcile upgraded to the house rule (an agreeing poll clears the optimistic override, one stale in-flight reply is tolerated, a second disagreement surrenders), replacing the older clear-on-every-poll shape, and the modal toolbar class renamed to the view-neutral `topology-inspview__toolbar`.

## [0.48.0] - 2026-07-21

### Added

- **Inspector no-node strip: a third **Stats** ("hot nodes") modal beside Runtime/Timeline.** A per-node grid of NAME / COUNTER / LGST_MSG / READ / WRITTEN, read from the `dump_metadata` graph the console already polls each tick (no new poll for the baseline), rendered with the sortable grid extracted out of the Runtime view into a shared module both views now consume. It mounts its own `runtime_stats` poller only while open (the Runtime view's exact pattern) to join Router profiling: `runtime_stats` now also returns `profiles` (per-node `{ name, avg, time, count }`) and `profiles_total` — both `null` while profiling is disabled — derived from `Router_Node::profiles()` / `RouterNode.profiles()` with identical keys across the PHP and JS runtimes; `list_profiles`'s text output is untouched (Tachikoma REPL parity). When profiling is off the modal shows a compact **Enable profiling** toggle that fires `profile on` into the viewed scope (`_cwd`) down the same interpreter path the poller uses; when on, it shows **Disable profiling** (firing `profile off`) and joins AVG / TIME / COUNT onto the grid by node name. The toggle flips **optimistically** — its label + highlight swap at click and reconcile to the next poll's truth (the Trace-button self-heal), instead of waiting on the profiles dataset. Column totals ride the grid's own `<tfoot>` (aligned to the columns by construction, out of the sortable body): COUNTER / READ / WRITTEN summed, LGST_MSG maxed, and — when profiling is on — AVG / TIME / COUNT from `profiles_total`, NAME reading `--total--`. The strip button is relabeled **Profiler** (matching the modal title) so it no longer collides with the pre-existing `stats` verb button, and the no-node strip gains a **profiles** (`list_profiles`) command button. Its sibling **Runtime** modal gains a matching all-nodes **Trace** toggle with the identical optimistic treatment — firing `trace` at `*` (`debug_state * <level>` + metadata `optimisticPatchAll`) and self-healing against the metadata poll.
- **The topology palette now renders through a `.topology-palette-dock` wrapper, structurally identical to `.topology-inspector-dock`.** The palette used to be a single `<aside class="topology-palette">` that owned its own grid placement, border, and collapsed rail, with the toggle chevron nested inside it — so its margin/padding composed differently from the inspector's. It is now an outer `.topology-palette-dock` (grid cell, right-edge border, `overflow: hidden`, `--collapsed` rail) holding the `topology-palette__toggle` chevron and the `<aside class="topology-palette">` as sibling direct children; the aside keeps only its own top-padding + scroll (the chevron-clearing `padding: 32px 0 0` mirrors the inspector). The three render branches collapse into one dock, the dead `topology-palette--collapsed` / `topology-palette__toggle--collapsed` variants are gone, and the toggle's aria/title conventions match the inspector. Purely structural — search, sections, drag, and collapse behavior are unchanged.
- **One plugin-wide focus-ring policy replaces the scattered per-component rings.** Every interactive element (button, input, select, textarea, link, `[tabindex]`) across every surface this plugin renders — topology console, debug overlay, devtools hub, event dashboards, vault + aggregator tabs, the admin settings page, and the shared tab host / connection banner — now gets ONE shared treatment from `src/shared/styles/_focus.scss` (imported by each surface's entry stylesheet): a visible ring on `:focus-visible` (keyboard / programmatic) in `var(--ink, currentColor)`, and NO ring on a plain mouse `:focus` (which also suppresses wp-admin's / emotion's blue glow). The per-component `:focus` / `:focus-visible` outline one-offs — search input, add-chip, edit-row inputs, REPL input, modal close, dashboard card-link, devtools tab host, timeline input, and the shared `_controls` input ring — are removed and unified into that policy; non-ring focus cues (border-color changes) and decorative selection outlines are untouched. Scoped under the plugin's root containers so wp-admin chrome outside our surfaces is unaffected.

- **Timer FIRES counts actual emits, not driven ticks.** `fire_cb` now increments `fire_count`/`fireCount` after the hitchhike throttle gate (and never without a sink), so `list_timers`, `runtime_stats`, and the Runtime modal report real work — the old every-tick climb made throttled hitchhikers look busy (obvious once the Runtime grids rendered it). JS also renames `fire_count` to the idiomatic `fireCount`. Spinner detection is unaffected: an own-slot spinner has no throttle gate, so its count still climbs every tick.

- **`Tail_Node` follows a single filename with `tail -F` logrotate semantics — a second source shape beside today's segmented `{file}.{seg}` mode.** A new fourth argument `source_mode` (`segmented` default, or `file`) selects the shape and fails loud (errors-as-docs) on anything else; the segmented behavior is untouched. File mode holds the open handle and, each poll, reads appended bytes, drains a rotated-away generation to EOF before reopening the path from offset 0 (no lost tail-end), resets on an in-place truncation, and tolerates a missing path — reusing the shared `Buffered_Pump` line-assembly (partial-line buffering, per-line emit) and the durable offsetlog cursor. The single-file cursor rides the SAME frame shape as segments: the inode occupies the container slot where a segment id sits (`<inode>:<offset>:<length>`), so there is no new field or parallel format. A resume validates the persisted cursor against the current file — inode match, then `size >= cursor`, then a line-boundary check that the byte before the cursor is a newline — and restarts from offset 0 on any mismatch (at-least-once, never cross-generation hunting). `dump_config` round-trips the mode + path.

- **Router profiling — Tachikoma's Router self-timing + `list_profiles`, ported to both runtimes behind a single `profile [on|off]` verb.** When enabled, `_router` times every dispatch and keeps a per-node self-time table (a nested dispatch's elapsed is subtracted from its parent's open frame, so times are self, not cumulative — Tachikoma Router.pm's push/pop stack, balanced via `finally` even when a fill throws poison or `Worker_Should_Stop`). One `profile` verb toggles or sets it: bare `profile` toggles (off↔on), explicit `profile on` / `profile off` is an idempotent set (the form scripts + UI use, so a caller that knows its desired state never races a stale toggle) — preserving Tachikoma's reply strings (`profiling enabled`/`disabled`, `already enabled`/`disabled`). This collapses Tachikoma's `enable_profiling` / `disable_profiling` pair into one toggle — a deliberate divergence (debug_state-precedent). `list_profiles [glob]` renders AVERAGE/TIME/COUNT/WINDOW/RATE/AGE/WHAT slowest-average-first with a `--total--` row; the special glob `total` prints only the total. Entries idle past 900 s are trimmed each router tick. Profiling off costs one null-check per dispatch; PHP and JS twins share identical semantics and a scriptable clock seam.
- **Topology console + overlay: a Runtime + Timeline view cluster opened from the Inspector's no-node strip.** The `_command_interpreter` inspector panel gains two buttons — **Runtime** and **Timeline** — each opening ONE wide modal (the inspector rail is too narrow for grids). *Runtime* mounts a `Dmesg` poller (verb `runtime_stats`, target `_cwd` — browser-local at root, the cd'd worker when pivoted) only while the modal is open and renders the Event_Framework's registered timers + cURL/EventSource handles as two click-to-sort grids (numeric columns sort numerically); a drain spinner — a timer due every tick (`NEXT <= 0`) whose `FIRES` keep climbing across polls — is flagged with a red row + a ⚠ marker. `runtime_stats` returns `{ timers, handles }` as keyed rows (`{id, active, interval_ms, mode, next_ms, oneshot, fires, type, name}` / `{id, count, type, name}`), from which the existing `list_timers`/`list_handles` text tables also derive — one source of truth, PHP and JS; `Dmesg.fill()` now also publishes an object reply payload (as `reply`) alongside its string-tail path, and takes a configurable verb + arguments. *Timeline* renders the DEBUG traces already flowing into the console transcript (a node with `debug_state` on emits `DEBUG: <event> <payload>` on every `set_state()`; the Inspector's Trace button toggles it per node) as a filterable time / node / event / payload table, newest-last, with case-insensitive node + event substring filters and a fixed header outside the one scrollable body (the scrollbar stays beside the rows). It is a parsed VIEW over the SAME `_output` transcript the console already holds, read directly off the node state — no new nodes, verbs, or polling — so it works identically in the topology console and the debug overlay Console tab, local or cd'd. This supersedes the earlier standalone Runtime/Logs devtools tabs and the transcript's Text|Timeline toggle.
- **New `taillog` root verb — a bounded server-log tail (REPL-reachable, no UI yet).** `taillog <source> [max_kb]` returns the last `min(max_kb, 64)`KB (default 16) of a durable aggregated log FILE, the partial first line dropped: `source` is a NAME from a fixed registry (`php` → `ini_get('error_log')` when it names a real file; `debug` → `WP_CONTENT_DIR/debug.log`) — never a caller path, so there is no traversal. The registry is **deduped by realpath**, so where php `error_log` IS `wp-content/debug.log` (e.g. `WP_DEBUG_LOG` hosts) the two collapse to one entry (`php`, the ini-configured aggregation point, wins) instead of listing identical content twice. `taillog` with no source lists the registry with per-source availability + byte size; the reserved name **`taillog sources`** returns the deduped registry as a `{ name, path, available }` struct (array reply, like `dump_metadata`); a missing/unreadable file returns a teaching error naming the resolved path.
- **Topology console: TSL export/import affordances on the header.** Live (view) mode gains a **SAVE** button that snapshots the on-screen graph — it captures the live graph's `dump_config` output (reusing the Dumper transcript round-trip via a new one-shot `DumperNode.captureNextReply`, which works for a live worker AND the browser-local graph) and hands it to the existing save-name prompt. Edit mode gains **DOWNLOAD** (writes the current editor draft out as `<topology-name>.tsl` via a Blob object URL) and **UPLOAD** (a `.tsl` file picker that loads the chosen file's text into the editor draft, marking it dirty like a typed edit). SAVE keeps a stable header slot across modes; DOWNLOAD/UPLOAD are edit-only and hidden in the debug overlay.
- **Palette search + Messages panel polish.** The node palette (topology console AND overlay console) gains a search input filtering the class list case-insensitively by shell name and description — doubling as the node-schema catalog lookup, since every tile already carries its schema. The overlay Overview's Messages panel is relabeled "Messages (this browser)", renders a relative age per line, and gains err/warn/dbg level-filter chips; the list's memo now keys on a monotonic per-push sequence, so a same-instant burst at ring capacity can no longer leave the panel stale.

- **`docs/upgrading.md` — a curated breaking-changes page for consumer-plugin authors.** One entry per consumer-facing contract change (topology args, verb tables, wire shapes, JS runtime globals), the fix beside each, seeded with the 0.47.x breaks. Standing rule recorded in the doc: a release that breaks a consumer contract adds its entry in the same commit as its CHANGELOG entry. Linked from the doc map's Reference bucket and README's Status section.
### Changed

- **The Inspector's no-node strip is normalized into three visually separated groups — Views / Toggles / Commands — with real two-state toggles.** The strip used to interleave modal-openers, stateful buttons, and stateless verb-dumps in one flat grid. It now groups them under small mono headers (`.topology-insp__group-label`, styled from the strip's existing treatment): **Views** opens a modal (Runtime, Profiler, Timeline, Compose); **Toggles** are single stateful buttons (Trace, Profiling, Verbose); **Commands** are the stateless `[label, verb]` transcript-dumps (dmesg, config, metadata, stats, timers, handles, profiles, ping, debug). The **Profiling** toggle replaces the old `profile on` / `profile off` command pair with one button that fires `profile on`/`profile off` per its current state, reading its truth from a new `_header.profiling` field in the `dump_metadata` snapshot the console already polls (`Router_Node::profiles()` / `RouterNode.profiles()` null-check, both runtimes) and self-healing exactly like Trace; it flips optimistically at click. The **Verbose** toggle replaces the old `debug_level 2` command button with one button that flips `debug_level` 2 ↔ 0 through the console's LOCAL dispatch, reading the live level from a reactive mirror of the Dumper verbosity dial (threaded from the topology console and the debug overlay). The Stats modal + its Views button are renamed **Profiler** (the `stats` verb button — a different thing — stays in Commands). Applies identically in the topology console and the debug-overlay Console tab (shared Inspector).
- **The no-node **Trace** button now behaves like the per-node one — immediate highlight, label swap, explicit level.** It fired a raw `debug_state *` command with no state reflection: the highlight only followed on the next `dump_metadata` poll and the label never changed. It now fires the `trace` action at `*` with an explicit level (0/1), optimistically patching every node's `debug_state` in the local graph so the button highlights and its label swaps to "stop trace" at once — matching the per-node Trace button.
- **`debug_state *` replies with a terse one-line summary instead of a per-node roster.** The `*` branch (both runtimes) returned `Setting all nodes to debug_state: <n>` followed by one `<name> debug_state: <n>` line per node — deliberately verbose since 0.22.0; it now returns `debug_state <level> on <N> nodes`, superseding that. The roster is one `ls` away. `list_profiles`, no-arg `debug_state`, and single-node `debug_state` replies are unchanged.
- **The CommandInterpreter `debug_state` verb is renamed to `trace` (both runtimes, no alias).** The per-node/interpreter trace toggle — `trace [ <node> [ <level> ] ]`, with the same bare / `<node>` / `*` forms — is now `trace`; the old `debug_state` name returns unknown-command. The UI has labelled this **Trace** everywhere since the strip normalization, and `debug_state` vs the Dumper's `debug_level` name-adjacency invited exactly the confusion the rename removes — a deliberate Tachikoma divergence. The `debug_state` node *property*, its `dump_metadata` field, and the reply strings that report it are unchanged. `docs/upgrading.md` carries the one-line consumer note.
- **The no-node strip's `debug` button is a `debug_level` 0↔1 toggle in the Toggles group — the sibling of Verbose on one dial.** It used to sit in Commands as a stateless dump of the bare `debug_level` verb. It now lives beside Verbose as a two-state button (`debug` / `stop debug`) reading the same reactive `debug_level` truth Verbose does: `debug` lit at level ≥ 1, `verbose` at ≥ 2 (verbose lit implies debug lit — one dial, not two switches). Clicking `debug` fires `debug_level 1` when below 1 and `debug_level 0` at or above it (collapsing the whole dial); Verbose keeps its `debug_level 2` / `debug_level 0` behavior. Synchronous LOCAL dispatch, so no optimistic override is needed.
- **README's Status section states what is settled instead of promising renames.** The old line hardcoded a version (already one release stale) and told adopters to "expect schema-field renames." It now names the settled load-bearing contracts (`fill()`, the 7-field message, sink/target routing — ADR-1/2/7), confines pre-1.0 movement to the edges (verb tables, schema fields), and points at `docs/upgrading.md` for the curated break list.
- **Shipped retention defaults now bound disk growth: `min_lifetime` 86400 → 900, `max_lifetime` 0 → 86400.** The old pair reproduced the legacy 2-seg/24h behavior: count-pruning couldn't fire until a segment was a full day old (an unbounded-growth window under sustained writes) and the age rule was disabled outright. A partition's oldest segments are now count-prune eligible after 15 minutes, and anything older than 24 hours is pruned down to `min_segments` regardless of count.

### Fixed

- **`Message::packed()` no longer destroys a frame carrying invalid UTF-8.** A VALUE with a bare non-UTF-8 byte (e.g. a logged SQL string built from a latin1 column) made `wp_json_encode()` return `false`, which `packed()` silently coerced to `''` — an empty wire frame a consumer's `unpacked('')` then rejected with a misleading "expected a 7-element positional array" error, three steps removed from the real cause. `packed()` now passes `JSON_INVALID_UTF8_SUBSTITUTE` so the bad byte is substituted (U+FFFD) instead of destroying the whole frame; a genuinely unencodable message (recursion depth, INF/NAN) now logs and emits a well-formed TM_ERROR frame instead of `''`. `Message::unpacked()` now distinguishes a JSON decode failure (names `json_last_error_msg()`) from a shape failure (wrong element count/list-ness), both with a bounded excerpt of the offending data.
- **The same silent-swallow shape existed at two more call sites in this plugin; both now substitute rather than lose data.** `Grep_Node::fill()`'s array-VALUE stringify fallback and `Node::drop_message()`'s payload-diagnostic formatter both used a bare `(string)` cast around `wp_json_encode()`, which coerces an encode failure to `''` — in `Grep_Node` that silently dropped a message that should have matched its filter (default pattern `.` never matches an empty string); in `drop_message()` it printed a blank `payload: ` on the very audit line meant to explain a drop. Both now pass `JSON_INVALID_UTF8_SUBSTITUTE`.
- **The Timeline view no longer swallows the envelope's trailing `}` into a payload under verbose (`debug_level 2`).** A verbose transcript entry is the Dumper's multi-line envelope dump with the DEBUG trace riding its `value:` line; the `DEBUG_TRACE` regex captured the payload with `[\s\S]*$`, crossing the newline to grab the envelope's closing brace (the stray ` }` at the end of the payload cell). The parse is now line-scoped: it splits the entry, finds the line carrying the `DEBUG:` marker, and parses node / event / payload from that line alone (payload capture is `.*`, never crossing a newline). The node for such a line is the space-free token immediately before ` DEBUG:`.
- **The verbose (`debug_level 2`) envelope dump no longer wedges a blank line before `}`.** A VALUE ending in a newline left the Dumper's `value:` field with a trailing indented empty line; the value is now trimmed of its trailing newline so exactly one newline separates it from the closing brace. Fixed identically in both runtimes (`src/runtime/dumper-node.js`, `includes/class-dumper-node.php`).

## [0.47.1] - 2026-07-16

### Changed

- **Retired the `Core.reinit` global; the overlay Reset-Graph capability is now the `Core.rebuildable` boolean.** `Core.reinit` was a function reference `mountExospine` stashed but never invoked — the Inspector only read it as a `!! reinit` truthiness check, and the actual dashboard reset already runs through `Core.bumpGraphGeneration()` (a reused mount's `spine.reinit` is subscribed to it). `mountExospine` now sets `Core.rebuildable = true` in the same owner-build-delegated condition; `InspectorTab` reads it; the returned `spine.reinit` handle is unchanged. Dashboard Reset-Graph tests now drive the real generation-bump path.
- **Schema-argument token defaults now fail loud on an unresolvable token.** `Core::resolve_config_token()` / `resolve_config_tokens()` gained a `$strict` flag and `Schema_Reflection::resolve_default()` resolves schema `<ns:key>` defaults strictly: an unknown namespace, a resolver that returns `null` (key not owned by its namespace), or a non-scalar now throws instead of silently coercing to `''`. This catches the wrong-namespace footgun where a `bool` default silently became `false`. Shell/TSL interpolation and the GC / workers-CI path-resolution callers stay non-strict (Tachikoma parity: an unset `<var>` / unowned `<ns:key>` still interpolates to `''`). A missing bundled geometry key (e.g. `<config:segment_size>`) — previously coerced to a dangerous `0` — now throws at node construction; owned-but-empty keys (an unset `<eln:stats_mirror_node>`) still resolve to `''` and never throw.
- **`Command_Interpreter_Node` (JS) documents its `arguments` coercion as an explicit external-compatibility seam** — it guards a non-array `arguments` arriving from an older/foreign wire client, not first-party producers (which emit a token array and are asserted).

### Removed

- **Removed `Aggregator_CI`'s dead `status`, `health`, and `servers` verbs** (and their `cmd_status` / `cmd_health` / `cmd_servers` handlers). The live hub dashboard reads only the de-god slices `summary` + `servers_status`; the raw keyed `status` snapshot, the `health` probe, and the legacy `servers` list had zero production callers. The shared `build_snapshot()` engine stays, and its cache-miss / partition-fan-out / node-discovery / Vault-reach coverage moved onto the `servers_status` tests.
- **`Config_Utils::is_within()`** (a `@deprecated` path-containment helper) and the ignored `$allowed_dirs` parameter on `Config_Utils::validate_config_path()`. `is_within()` carried an `@api` "external consumers" tag but had zero callers anywhere in the checkout; `$allowed_dirs` was documented "ignored" and both callers passed a no-op `[DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR]`. No runtime behavior change; noted here because `is_within()` was a published-API surface.

## [0.47.0] - 2026-07-16

### Changed

- **TM_COMMAND `arguments` and node-constructor `arguments` are now a flat token array (`list<string>` argv) end to end, instead of a single space-joined string.** Tokenization happens ONCE at the producer boundary (the Shell / REST command builder), the tokens are carried verbatim through the command envelope, the interpreter, and `make_node`, and they only re-join into a line at the single serialization anchor (`Node::serialize_args()` / the JS `serializeArg`). The old design tokenized → joined → re-split several times and lost quote grouping, so a quoted `cmd x verb 'a b'` reached the verb handler as two arguments; it now arrives as one token. `Command_Args::parse()` takes `list<string>` and `format()` returns `list<string>` (no more embedded quoting/unescaping); verb handlers receive `array $args` and read `$args[0]`, `$args[1]`, … ; `Node::arguments()` / `parse_schema_args()` take and return token arrays; `dump_config()` round-trips through `serialize_args()`. TM_INFO / TM_REQUEST / TM_BYTESTREAM VALUEs remain flat strings — only the structured `{name, arguments}` command envelope changed. The HMAC canonical (`Command_Auth`) signs the arguments array. PHP and JS runtimes mirror each other exactly.

- **The Shell tokenizer gained backslash-escape support, so `serialize_args()` / `serializeArg` are now lossless for ANY token.** Inside a quote, `\` escapes the next char (PHP `Shell_Node::tokenize` + `split_statements`, JS `tokenize` + `splitStatements`); serialization quotes a token containing whitespace, a quote char (`'`/`"`/`` ` ``), a backslash, or an empty string, escaping `\` and the wrapping `'`. Previously a node argument carrying a quote char or an empty positional slot round-tripped wrong through `dump_config` (the empty slot vanished and later args shifted position). The JS `quoteToken` (send_struct JSON) now delegates to `serializeArg` and is never "unrepresentable". `CommandClient.buildMessage()` and `Node.command()` now **throw** on a non-array `args` instead of silently coercing to `[]`.

### Fixed

- **Fixed a console crash on node-select and an empty-name error on topology activate/save/delete/get, both from the token-array cutover.** The Inspector fed the now-array `node.arguments` into a string helper (`( raw || '' ).trim()` → `TypeError: .trim is not a function`); it now consumes the token array directly. And the topology-console's `useLayout` / `useSaveTopology` / `useDeleteTopology` / `useTopologyList` / `useExpandedIncludes` / activate hooks built their command `args` as hand-rolled strings, which `buildMessage` silently coerced to `[]` — so the server saw an empty name and threw `invalid name: must match …`. They now build argv with `formatCommandArgs(...)` like every other command producer.

- **The console's static TSL parsers now accept everything the runtime Shell does: line continuations, cd cwd-pathing, and the make/connect/command aliases.** `Topology_Registry` (PHP, feeding `expand()` / `statements()` / `graph_for()`) and `parseTsl` (JS) each read a topology file line-by-line and understood only `make_node`/`connect_node`/`disconnect_node`/`cmd`/`include` at column zero. A real `.tsl` that split a `make_node` across backslash-continued lines, grouped config verbs in a `cd <node>:config` … `cd ..` block, or used the `make`/`connect`/`command`/`command_node` aliases parsed wrong — dropped ctor args, missing config-target edges, uncaptured verbs — so the console graph diverged from what the worker actually builds (and, with the borrowed-verbs inspector, showed the wrong checkboxes). Both parsers now share a normalization pass mirroring `Shell_Node`: backslash continuations join, `command`/`command_node` canonicalize to `cmd`, and `cd`/`chdir` cwd resolves so a bare or explicit command line becomes `cmd <cwd-resolved-path> <verb> <args>`. A shared `tests/fixtures/request-builder.tsl` drives both test suites against identical input.

- **The topology console inspector now shows a borrowed node's config verbs, read-only.** Selecting an included node in edit mode rendered its constructor args but dropped the whole Verbs section, so you couldn't see which checkboxes (`void_warranty`, `allow_large_writes`, `with_index`, …) an included topology had ticked. The root cause was two layers: `Topology_Registry::expand()` never carried a node's config verbs in its record (only `make_node` args and `set_*target` edges), and `LockedForm` had no Verbs section. `expand()` now collects each `cmd <node>[:config] <verb> <args>` into a `verbs` field (a `set_*target` still resolves to an edge, not a verb), the console maps it into the borrowed node's `verbInvocations`, and the inspector renders it read-only — disabled checkboxes for single verbs (ticked to match) and a row per invocation for `multiple` verbs. Editing a borrowed node's config stays where it belongs: the source topology.

## [0.46.2] - 2026-07-15

### Fixed

- **Long-lived dashboards recover their WordPress session when a tab becomes visible again.** `SseInNode` now treats visibility as a direct resumptive reconnect signal instead of depending on a React hidden-state commit or a background-throttled watchdog, and a terminal page-local stream renews the REST nonce before reopening at the exact saved offset. Each failed connection cycle gets one renewal; another terminal rejection falls back to the existing reconnect throttle until a real `CONNECTED` handshake or a new visibility wake-up, preventing permanent 404/429/CORS failures from spinning. Page-local `CommandClient`s use the same single-flight renewal and retry an invalid-nonce POST once, so non-SSE dashboard actions recover without a reload, while explicitly configured remote credentials are never replaced with the local site's nonce. Explicitly closed/paused streams remain closed.

## [0.46.1] - 2026-07-15

### Fixed

- **`wp nodes run` no longer declares a `--quiet` option.** It shadowed WP-CLI's built-in global `--quiet`, so WP-CLI warned at registration ("registering an argument '--quiet' that conflicts with a global argument of the same name"). Quiet is delegated to the global flag — WP-CLI's Quiet logger already suppresses the `log`/`success` output — so the command drops its redundant synopsis entry and manual guard.

## [0.46.0] - 2026-07-15

### Fixed

- **Config and test entry points no longer assume a particular container checkout.** The operator-controlled `LOCAL_NEWSPACK_NODES_CONF` override accepts any canonical readable PHP file instead of restricting it to the active plugin or WordPress roots, and an invalid explicit path or return value now fails loudly instead of silently loading site defaults. The shared validator retains its published three-argument call shape so Nodes and its independently released consumers can be upgraded in either order; its former containment primitive remains available as a deprecated compatibility helper. `tests/run.sh` runs the vendor PHPUnit for its own checkout, and the AI Newsletter example's coverage path is relative to its PHPUnit config.

- **Browser `RemoteLink` and `RemoteIpc` palette drops are viable channels.** Connecting a dropped `RemoteLink` output now opens its configured SSE subscription, disconnecting closes it, and replaying its `dump_config` restores both the non-default subscription and edge before reopening. `RemoteIpc` now treats its required `reader` argument as the remote worker address instead of silently substituting the local canvas node name, preserves that reader through dump/replay, and stamps its own local name on the minted `connect_worker_input`. Missing `subscribe`/`reader` arguments fail during `make_node` and clean up the half-built node, while owner-tagged shared heartbeat slots prevent an inactive channel from stopping its active sibling's keepalive. Its existing address-channel canvas shape remains intentional: commands reach it by Router/name rather than a direct input edge, while its output edge owns the inherited stream connection lifecycle.
- **Config-target graph edges resolve topology tokens before they are folded.** A configured `cmd … set_*target <namespace:key>` now points at the resolved node in dashboard graphs, topology-console include baselines, and standalone topology seeds; own nodes remain editable instead of being recast as borrowed just to carry the resolved edge. Top-level token overrides on borrowed nodes use the resolved target while editing but retain the raw token when saved, and an empty resolution clears only that named config slot. Missing seed-resolution metadata now surfaces as a console error instead of disappearing in the seed promise. This lets the event logger's configured flame-stats mirror render beneath `flame-builder` instead of as a disconnected root.
- **Static topology graphs and console reopen state now mirror runtime connection semantics.** Regular Nodes keep one `connect_node` target (a later connect replaces it), and either form of `disconnect_node` clears that connection without erasing independent `cmd … set_*target` routing; repeating one config setter replaces that slot while distinct setters coexist, and an empty setter clears only its named slot. Tees still accumulate/deduplicate targets, remove only an explicitly named target, and treat a one-argument disconnect as the Shell's FROM-targeted operation rather than “clear all.” Multi-root expansion now evaluates shared nested includes once while retaining every top-level provenance path. The include baseline carries node Tee-ness plus connect/config edge roles, and console parsing preserves routing statement order, so reopening `combined` does not resurrect its disconnected direct edges; top-level config overrides on borrowed nodes retain their named slot through include rebases, save, and reopen; config-only routing is not offered or serialized as a removable connection; and own Tap/custom Tee nodes fan out according to the class catalog. Worker graph reconstruction filters repeated handlers by their concrete nearest upstream log/source, so each visual branch shows only its own `P0`/read-rate badge even when Tee branches converge.
- **Topology seeds now wait for the PHP class catalog.** Opening or editing a topology, including the pre-metadata seed used when a worker is down, can no longer race `classes.list` and permanently collapse an own Tap/custom Tee's fan-out using regular-node semantics. Catalog request and response-shape failures leave the seed gated and surface the actual error.

### Added

- **The browser REPL now supports `help <class>` with PHP parity.** JavaScript node classes render the same category, description, capability flags, constructor arguments, commands, requests, registrations, defaults, and aligned sections as the PHP command interpreter instead of reporting a valid canvas class as an unknown help topic.
- **Delete removes a selected hull's include.** A hull IS the include, so it now answers Delete/Backspace like a selected node or edge does — no round trip to the inspector's include tree. Only a DIRECTLY-declared include can go (a nested one has no `include` line in this topology to remove), and only in edit mode, since removing an include edits the draft. The selection clears with it.

## [0.45.3] - 2026-07-14

### Fixed

- **A failing `/command` POST reported itself as a ghost, not as an HTTP error.** `CommandClient` never checked `r.ok`, so a non-2xx response — whose body is a WordPress REST error OBJECT, not JSONL — went through `unpack()`, which minted a blank message, which routed into the graph and surfaced three hops later as `_router: WARNING: message not addressed`. Seen live: the `_heartbeat` node POSTing into a **404 `rest_no_route`** while the plugin was briefly deactivated mid-deploy. An expired nonce (**401 `rest_forbidden`**) would have done the same — every command silently becoming a ghost instead of saying the session had expired.

  It now names the failure: `ERROR: CommandClient: /command failed - HTTP 404 rest_no_route`.

## [0.45.2] - 2026-07-14

### Changed

- **Header button order is fixed and consistent across modes** — live: `NEW OPEN EDIT LIVE`; edit: `NEW OPEN SAVE DELETE SETTINGS EDIT LIVE`. Live is a strict PREFIX of edit, so no control moves under the cursor when you switch. Previously NEW was rendered twice (once per mode) and landed AFTER the edit-only buttons in live, while SETTINGS sat before DELETE.

### Fixed

- **OPEN no longer appears in the debug overlay**, which has no editor to open a topology into — a regression from making OPEN available in live mode. NEW and OPEN are both gated on the overlay now, as NEW already was.

## [0.45.1] - 2026-07-14

### Fixed

- **Found the `_router: WARNING: message not addressed - TYPE_UNKNOWN` ghost.** It was not a buggy minter — it was the wire. `unpack()` returns a fresh blank message for any line that is not a 7-field array, and `CommandClient` fed EVERY line of a `/command` response straight back into the graph (`HttpOut` fills each reply into its sink). So one malformed response line became a message with no TYPE, no FROM and no TO, which is precisely what `_router` was reporting.

  The wire boundary now rejects it — a line `unpack()` cannot read is dropped with `ERROR: CommandClient: dropped an unparseable /command response line`, naming the real fault instead of surfacing a ghost three hops downstream. The guard sits in the shared `#post`, so `send()` and `postBatch()` are both covered. `SseInNode` already did this for its own ingress; the command path never did.

## [0.45.0] - 2026-07-14

### Added

- **`TM_UNTYPED` (1024) — the mint default for a message.** `new_message()` used to hand back `TYPE = 0`, so a message that was minted and never typed was indistinguishable in the drop audit from a naked array with no TYPE at all. Both printed `TYPE_UNKNOWN`, and a live `_router: WARNING: message not addressed - TYPE_UNKNOWN` told you nothing about which. Now a minted-but-untyped message reports `TM_UNTYPED` (our bug) and a naked array still reports `TYPE_UNKNOWN` (garbage).

  It is a free HIGH bit, so it matches NO type gate — an untyped message is inert. A `-1` sentinel would have been the opposite: as a bitmask every bit is set, so it would satisfy `type & TM_COMMAND` AND `type & TM_EOF` AND `type & TM_ERROR` at once, and be acted on by every handler in the graph.

  Both runtimes mint it (PHP `Message::TM_UNTYPED`, JS `TM_UNTYPED`) — it is part of the wire format, so they move together.

### Fixed

- **`SseInNode` dropped malformed frames via `! message[ TYPE ]`**, which the new truthy mint default would have silently defeated — malformed frames would have been ROUTED. It now splits the two causes it had been conflating: `unpack()` returns a fresh (untyped) message when a frame will not parse, so `TM_UNTYPED` means the WIRE was garbage (`unparseable frame`), while a clean 7-field frame carrying no type is a different bug (`typeless frame`). Separate ERROR states, separate rate-limit keys.

## [0.44.1] - 2026-07-14

### Fixed

- **Drilling into a hull did nothing in live mode.** "Open request-builder.tsl" loaded the topology into the DRAFT but never left view mode, so the canvas kept rendering the live graph and the button looked inert. It now lands you in the editor, like New already does.

### Added

- **OPEN is available in live mode**, not just edit. It was gated to edit mode, which is precisely why opening a topology never needed to switch modes — same root as the hull bug. Picking a topology from live now opens it in the editor. SAVE stays edit-only; there is no draft to save from live.

## [0.44.0] - 2026-07-14

### Fixed

- **The borrowed-node lock vanished on the first `dump_metadata` poll in live mode.** A node's provenance (`origin` — which include provides it) lives in the parsed tsl; metadata nodes carry none. The lock badge read it straight off the node, so it painted on entry from the parsed graph and disappeared the moment the first poll swapped in metadata nodes. Provenance is now stamped onto the canvas graph from the expand baseline — the same membership map the hulls are drawn from, which is why the hulls never had this bug — so the lock, the Inspector's borrowed state, and the hulls can no longer disagree.

- **The lock badge overlapped the liveness LED.** 12px type start-anchored at `NODE_W - 26` runs to `NODE_W - 14`; the LED's left edge is `NODE_W - 15.5`. Moved to `NODE_W - 32`, and a test pins the clearance rather than the magic number.

- **Dark skins drew a near-black caret on a near-black select.** The chevron is a baked data-URI (an SVG background cannot read a CSS var), dark by default, with a rule repainting it light for the seven dark skins. That rule was written `.topology-app.topology-app.newspack-nodes-theme.theme-crt` — all four classes on ONE element — but the skin class lives on `<html>` (`shared/theme.js`), so it matched nothing. The base rule won, and every dark skin got the dark chevron. The same dead block carried `color-scheme: dark`, so dark skins were also drawing light native number-spinners and checkboxes.

  The selectors are ancestor-form now, and the console's duplicate `.topology-select` list is gone — it only existed because the shared rule was silently dead, and `.topology-select` is a `<select>` the shared rule reaches.

### Changed

- **A reader's offsetlog and dead-letter dirs are ARGUMENTS, with no derived fallback.** `Remote_Source` used to invent an implicit offsetlog dir (`<offsets_dir>/<name>.<remote_partition>`) and dead-letter dir (`<base>/deadletter/…`) when a topology declared none — the last splinter of the hardcode that [147] set out to remove. It meant an omitted dir silently kept checkpointing at a path the topology could not write (so it could not carry `<topology>`, and two fleets pulling one spoke partition shared a cursor), and it flatly contradicted the plugin's own `test_offsetlog_dir_defaults_to_empty`. Both dirs now follow Consumer's contract: empty means no cursor and no quarantine. **Every stock topology declares both** — a Consumer that omitted its dead-letter dir was silently dropping poison rather than quarantining it.

  With the derivation gone, the offsetlog and the dead-letter queue turn out to be one shape in two geometries: a named, patron-linked Partition a node owns, whose dir is an argument and whose sink is its patron's. That shape now lives once, in the `Sidecar` trait, behind a `*_dir()` / `*_name()` seam pair. `ensure_offsetlog_partition()` and `ensure_deadletter_sibling()` are gone, and `Remote_Source` keeps only the two names it genuinely qualifies by remote partition.

### Fixed

- **Retention was inert on every partition built with a bare segment count.** A live offsetlog dir held **249** segments where 10 were intended.

  The dual-rule retention split gave Partition four axes (`min_segments`, `max_segments`, `min_lifetime`, `max_lifetime`), but several internal partitions still passed only two or three. The omitted axes fall back to their schema defaults, and the inherited `<config:min_lifetime>` is the one that bites: the count rule refuses to prune anything *younger* than it, so it was blocked until segments aged past that floor. The ceiling becomes `min_lifetime / checkpoint_interval` — with a 24h floor and a 30s checkpoint, **2,880** segments. The 249 found on disk wasn't the plateau; it was just how far that worker had got. Worse, two callers passed a *duration* into the `max_segments` slot: the settings log said `2 86400`, licensing 86400 segments.

  Every internal partition now declares all four axes explicitly:
  - **offsetlog** (`Offsetlog_Cursor`): 10–30 keyframes, holding 5 minutes, pruning past 15.
  - **dead-letter** (`Dead_Letter_Queue`): 16 segments by count, no age rule.
  - **IPC scratch** (`Worker_Base::ipc_partition_args()`, now shared by Bootstrap, the REPL and `wp nodes cli`): 2 segments by count, no age rule.
  - **settings log**: 2 segments, with the day-long lifespan as the AGE rule where it belongs.
  - **`wp nodes ingest`**: the flag is now `--max_segments` (was `--num_segments`), and it finally *does* something — it previously inherited `<config:min_lifetime>`, which protected every freshly-ingested segment and made the flag a no-op.

  `ensure_offsetlog()` moved from `Time_Travel` to `Offsetlog_Cursor`, which owns the offsetlog and now owns its geometry too.

  The old tests passed throughout, because the test environment's `min_lifetime` defaults to 0 — pruning fired in tests and never in production. The new tests backdate segment mtimes (retention reads the real clock, not `Core::$now`) and assert both rules for real.

### Added

- **A selected hull now shows its own message and byte rates.** Activity (messages in/out per second, bytes read/written per second, as sparklines) and cumulative Throughput, scoped to the nodes that include provides — so an include's traffic is readable on its own, not just as part of the whole graph's.

  The roll-up goes through `processStats()`, the same source/sink accounting the process header uses: a hull's "in" is what its SOURCE nodes produced and its "out" is what its SINK nodes consumed, so a message hopping between two nodes *inside* the boundary isn't counted twice. One consequence is worth knowing: an include made only of pass-through nodes — no source, no sink — reads 0/0, because its traffic is interior to some other scope's boundary. The dmesg err/warn strip is deliberately omitted — those counts are process-wide, and showing them under one include's name would attribute the whole process to it.

  Nothing renders in edit mode: a draft graph has no counters, and the inspector already suppresses stats there rather than showing a permanently-zero panel.

  The sparklines show the history that *already happened*, not one that starts when you click. `useGraphRates` has been recording a 60-sample rate history for every node since page load, so the hull series is DERIVED from those per-node histories (`utils/aggregateSeries`) rather than accumulated from the moment of selection — select a hull and the last minute is already drawn. The trade-off is that a derived series is not a record: when a node leaves the graph its history goes with it, so the scope's older samples shrink to match.

  The stats presentation (`SparklineRow`, `ProcessStatsView`, the rate/byte formatters) moved out of `Inspector` into `components/ProcessStats`, and the shared `Section`/`FieldRow` layout primitives into `components/InspectorFields`, so `HullPanel` — which `Inspector` imports — can render the same view without an import cycle.

### Fixed

- **A SELECTED hull now highlights exactly like a hovered one** — members lit, inner wires lit, everything else faded. Selection is just the sticky form of the same focus gesture, so it gets the same treatment: hovering still takes over while the pointer is on a hull, and the selection reappears when you leave. Previously selection lit nothing, on the reasoning that lighting its members bought no contrast — but that was only true because selection didn't fade the rest either. It does now, so it does.

- **Dragging a hull didn't snap to the grid**, though dragging a single node always has. The hull committed the raw pointer delta, so a cluster moved by its hull landed wherever the mouse happened to stop.

  What snaps is the ANCHOR member's absolute target (the top-left-most one), and every member then moves by that one delta. The two obvious alternatives are both wrong: snapping each member's own position would quantise away the cluster's internal offsets and reshape the group you grabbed, while snapping the raw *delta* only preserves whatever offset the members already had — an off-grid cluster could never be tidied by dragging its hull, and since hull drags used to commit an unsnapped delta, those clusters are already out there in saved layouts. Anchoring gives both: the shape survives and the cluster lands on the grid.

  The live outline now previews the *snapped* delta too, so it clicks onto the grid as you drag instead of sliding out from under the cursor on release.

  The lattice lived in three hand-rolled copies (the palette drop's `snapToGrid`, plus inline half-step math in the node drag and, briefly, the hull drag). `snapPosition()` and `snapClusterDelta()` now sit beside `snapToGrid()` in `utils/autoLayout` and every drag path routes through them.

## [0.43.0] - 2026-07-13

### Added

- **`Remote_Source` reads like the Consumer it is [147]:** `vault_id`, `remote_partition`, **`offsetlog_dir`**, **`deadletter_dir`**. It used to HARDCODE both dirs (`Config::get_offsets_directory()`, and `<base>/deadletter`), which isn't just an asymmetry — it meant a topology could not write the cursor path, so the cursor could not carry `<topology>`, so two hubs pulling the same spoke partition would silently share one offsetlog. Every other Consumer got fleet-scoped cursors; this one structurally couldn't. Both args are optional (empty disables checkpointing / the DLQ, exactly like `Consumer`), and omitting them falls back to the legacy derived paths. `write_set()` reads the offsetlog from the ARGUMENT now rather than reconstructing it from the old convention — otherwise the conflict gate and the GC would both be looking at a cursor the node doesn't use.
- **`Topic` takes the Partition verbs: `allow_large_writes`, `void_warranty`, `with_index` [146].** The first two already existed as PHP methods but were unreachable — `Topic`'s `commands` was empty, so `cmd topic:config void_warranty` silently did nothing and the node never even wired a `{name}:config` interpreter. All three propagate to partitions the Topic materializes LATER (they're created lazily, on first write to a key), and `dump_config()` round-trips them like `Partition`'s does.

- **Hulls for NESTED includes, not just the directly-declared ones.** `expand()` now reports the node set of every topology in the tree at any depth, so `combined` draws `request-builder`, `flame-builder`, `job-router` AND `job-intake` — the last nested inside `job-router`. Outer hulls paint first, so a nested one lands on top of the parent that brings it.
- **Hull interaction.** Hovering a hull lights it and dims every node that isn't a member (on `combined`, hovering `job-intake` dims 14 of 16). Clicking a hull's FILL selects it — clicking a node inside it still selects the node, so the hull is never a scrim you have to fight past. Dragging a hull moves every member by one delta, so a borrowed cluster keeps its shape.
- **The hull inspector.** A hull is a composition boundary, not a node, so the panel shows what the canvas deliberately can't: the recursion we flattened out of the drawing (its include-tree), the nodes it provides, the ones an unrelated include ALSO provides (the diamond — visible on canvas only as an overlap; an ancestor or descendant sharing a node is containment, not sharing, and isn't named), and the edges crossing the boundary — the borrowed subsystem's interface. The action is **Open `<topology>`.tsl**: the hull is the handle for drilling in, and drilling in with an edited draft asks before dropping it, exactly like leaving edit mode.

### Fixed

- **A hovered hull read as a mix of opacities instead of one group.** Live-mode idle dimming applied to the hull's own members, and its internal wires kept the non-flowing edge dim — so hovering an idle include rendered it as part-dim boxes strung on faded wire, exactly the thing the hull exists to group. A hovered hull now lights: idle dimming is suspended on its members, and the edges wholly inside it drop the idle dim. Hover only — a hull stays SELECTED until you click away, so lighting on selection would hide live idle state indefinitely, and selection fades nothing, so it would buy no contrast anyway. Non-members fade to 0.4 (was 0.55), restoring the gap from the 0.7 idle dim that the hover fade is supposed to read against.
- **The palette showed its "Topologies" section in LIVE mode**, where there's no draft to `include` anything into — and it greyed entries from the stale edit `draft`, so a leftover include from an earlier edit session bled into the live view. The section is edit-only now, and the greying reads the mode-aware include set (the draft in edit, the viewed topology in live) instead of the draft unconditionally.
- **Clicking the background didn't clear a selected hull.** The canvas only treated a node or an edge as "a selection", so with only a hull selected the background click fell through to **autofit** instead of deselecting — and the hull panel stayed up. A hull is a selection: it now clears on a background click, and selecting a node or an edge supersedes it.
- **The topologies dashboard lost its segment colours** (consumer offset vs. TopicProbe offset vs. the live filesystem check — every bar went grey). Reader templates carry `<topology>` now, but the client substituted only `<partition>`, so `firehose.<topology>.p0` never matched the live reader `firehose.combined.p0`: no cursor, no colours, no read-rate badges. The client resolves both tokens, like `Topology_Loader` binds both.
- **Activity highlighting overrode the hull hover-dim.** `.topology-node` carries an entrance `animation` whose `both` fill locks opacity at 1, and a CSS animation beats a plain declaration — so an ACTIVE node ignored `.is-faded` entirely (`.is-idle` already cancels the animation for exactly this reason; the fade didn't). Same trap on a `--flowing` edge. Both now cancel the animation, and hovering a hull dims the non-member edges too.
- **A locked `Partition` leaked its `:heartbeat` Timer's router registration.** The Timer registers with `_router` for TIMER (only while the Event_Framework is draining — i.e. inside a worker, which is why no unit test caught it). Tearing the Partition down dropped the node from `Core` but left that registration pointing at a name that no longer resolved, so every tick the router walked a dangling entry: `_router: WARNING: jobintake.<pid>-<n>.p0:heartbeat forgot to unregister`, once per job (1,007 of them in the live log). `Partition::remove_node()` now removes the heartbeat AND the `:lock` sibling — the latter matters because `Job_Intake` names partitions with `pid + spl_object_id`, and PHP recycles `spl_object_id`, so a stale lock registration blocked the next `Job_Intake` from claiming its own name.

## [0.42.0] - 2026-07-13

### Added

- **A `<topology>` template token, bound to the FLEET.** An offsetlog is a reader's *cursor*, and the reader is the fleet — two processes tailing one log need two cursors. Without a token for "which fleet", two topologies that want to SHARE a reader when composed (`include` dedupes only byte-identical `make_node` lines) had to name the same offsetlog, which made them unsafe to run side by side. `<config:offsets_dir>/firehose.<topology>.p<partition>` resolves to `firehose.combined.p0` under `combined` and `firehose.request-builder.p0` when that topology runs standalone: identical declarations compose into one reader, distinct fleets get distinct cursors, and the conflict gate stays strict — a shared *log* is still a conflict, because only the cursor is fleet-scoped.

### Fixed

- **A broken include fails LOUD in the safety gates.** `write_set()` (which `find_conflicts` and `Log_Cleaner` read through) swallowed an unresolvable include and reported an empty write set — which reads as "no conflict" to the gate and "every one of its logs is an orphan" to the GC. A gate that quietly disarms itself is worse than no gate. `graph_for()` still degrades, since one bad `.tsl` must not take out the dashboard.

## [0.41.0] - 2026-07-13

### Fixed

- **A borrowed node is no longer painted as runtime drift.** `useCanonicalNodes` compared the live graph against the raw `.tsl`, so every node an `include` provided looked like a "temporary" node someone had `make_node`'d in by hand — for `combined.tsl` that was 15 of 16 nodes. A node an include declares is canonical; it's just declared in another file.
- **The console paints an include-based topology in one shot, without waiting for `dump_metadata`.** It seeds the canvas from the topology's `.tsl` before the first poll — but `parseTsl` on a file that mostly `include`s others yields only its own handful of nodes, so the canvas painted a sliver (`firehose:tee` + `_repl`) and everything else popped in on the next poll, which is exactly the staged paint autofit can't survive. The seed now expands its includes. And `topologies get` ships the COMPOSED graph (`includes` + `expanded`) alongside the file, so the first paint costs ONE round trip, not two — that second sequential fetch is what made an include-based topology feel slow next to a flat one.
- **Log retention no longer eats an included topology's logs.** `Log_Cleaner` drives off `resolved_resource_dirs()` → `write_set()`, which scanned the raw `.tsl` — so an include-only topology declared NOTHING and the GC saw its live logs and offsetlogs as orphans. (It takes one neighbour topology that DOES declare dirs to arm the sweep, which is every real fleet.) Now pinned by tests that fail loudly on the old code.
- **Static readers now understand `make` / `connect` / `disconnect`** — real aliases in the interpreter's verb table that topologies actually use (ELN's `performance.tsl` says `make Tee firehose:tee`). `expand()`, `graph_for()`, `write_set()`, and `segment_size_overrides_for()` only knew the long forms, so they painted a graph the runtime never builds.
- **`expand()` honors `disconnect_node`** (both the one-arg "clear the sink" and two-arg forms), applied in eval order. Without it the composed graph kept an edge a later `disconnect_node` had removed.
- **The `write_set` conflict gate saw through includes.** It scanned the raw file, so an include-only topology (ELN's `combined.tsl` is now two `include` lines) reported an EMPTY write set — silently disarming the gate that stops two fleets writing one log. `write_set()` and `segment_size_overrides_for()` now read the flattened statements, like `graph_for()`.
- **Flattened statements are memoized**, so a topology with includes doesn't re-walk (and re-read) its whole include tree on every static read. Invalidated on save.
- **Topology console: hulls no longer leak between topologies, and now render in live mode.** They were derived from `draft.includes`, which survives leaving edit mode — so an include dragged into one topology painted a hull over a *different* topology's live graph. Membership now comes from the expand baseline's provenance intersected with the nodes actually on screen, which also makes them work in live mode (where metadata nodes carry no `origin`).
- **Topology console: the whole graph appears at once.** `useGraphSource` counted the `_repl` scaffolding as "the graph has content", so the canvas laid out the scaffolding alone and every real node arriving on the next `dump_metadata` got tucked below it, in a column. View mode now waits for a real node.
- **Topology console: a freshly-opened topology with includes no longer reads as dirty** (leaving edit mode falsely prompted "discard unsaved changes?"). The async include reconcile rebuilt the node list in a different ORDER than the open path, and `applyLoadedBaseline` kept dangling baseline edges that `reconcileIncludes` dropped. Both now agree, and a no-op reconcile returns the same graph reference.

### Added

- **Topology console: a "Topologies" palette section — drag a whole topology onto the canvas to `include` it.** The drop is zero-config (an include takes no args, so no ctor modal), and self / an already-declared include / any ancestor grey out, so a drop that would form a cycle simply isn't offered. Borrowed nodes render desaturated and lock-badged under one translucent hull per declared include — hulls **overlap** where a node is shared, because "which include provides this node" is a set, not a container. The node is locked; its **wiring is not**: both handles stay live and every edge touching it is editable, borrowed-to-borrowed included, which is what lets you splice a filter between two borrowed endpoints. Deletion lives in the inspector's include-tree (top level removable, deeper levels read-only) alongside a per-node `via` breadcrumb. Saving writes the **collapsed** form: `include` lines, your own nodes, and `disconnect_node`/`connect_node` deltas against the expanded baseline.
- **`Topology_Registry::expand( array $include_names )` + the `topologies expand` verb.** Composes an include SET into one graph with provenance — `origin` (the directly-declared includes providing a node; a LIST, since a diamond-shared node has several) and `via` (the path it entered through) — plus the recursive include tree. Informational only: the runtime is still the Shell's `include`. It exists so the topology console can fetch its edit-mode baseline in ONE round trip instead of recursively fetching every included `.tsl`.
- **`topologies list` entries carry each topology's direct `includes`**, so a client can build the include DAG without a fetch per topology.
- **TSL `include <topology>` resolves through the topology registry.** `include` was a Shell builtin that took a file path; it now resolves a topology NAME the same way `Topology_Loader` does (user dir wins, then each stock dir), so a consumer plugin can compose the substrate's topology instead of copy-pasting a shadowing `.tsl` that drifts. A literal path still works for the REPL. Includes are memoized per top-level script (`#pragma once`), so two sibling includes reaching a shared base expand it exactly once — while a REPL that re-types `include foo` still re-runs the file. A cycle fails loud at worker boot (`Topology_Loader` sets the new `Shell_Node::fatal_on_cycle()`) but only logs in an interactive session, so a typo can't kill a live `wp nodes cli`.

### Fixed

- **`graph_for()` expands includes.** It line-scanned a single file, so a topology that included another read as an empty hole — and since `resolved_resource_dirs()` and `segment_size_overrides_for()` both derive from it, an included Partition's log dir would never have been created. It now walks the include tree (and degrades to an empty graph, logged, on a cycle or conflict — `dump_graph` visits every registered topology, so one broken `.tsl` must not take out the whole dashboard; the loader still fails loud at boot).
- **`topologies save` validates includes.** Its dry run only rejected an unterminated backslash continuation, so a body with an unknown include, a cyclic include, or a `make_node` that conflicts with one an include provides saved cleanly and then silently half-built (or killed) the worker at its next spawn. All three are now rejected at save.
- **`getTextColor()` in the shared format utils picks a badge's ink from its background luminance.** Dashboards that paint a chip with a hook-category color hardcoded white text, but 40 of the 63 shipped category colors are pale — `#CDDC39` (Options & Settings) sits at 1.5:1 against white and `#BDBDBD` (Sanitization/Localization) at 1.9:1, i.e. unreadable. The new util returns `#1e1e1e` or `#ffffff`, whichever wins on WCAG relative luminance, so operator-customized colors stay legible too.
- **`hexToRgba()` accepts 3-digit hex.** It sliced 6 digits unconditionally, so the shipped `#36F` (Newspack category) produced `rgba(NaN, NaN, NaN, …)` and the row tint silently dropped.

## [0.40.1] - 2026-07-13

### Fixed

- **Config-key declaration is PULLED on first read; a frontend request no longer fatals on a substrate config read.** `Bootstrap::ensure_runtime_wired()` used to be the only thing that called `Config::register_keys()`, but it deliberately runs on admin / REST / WP-CLI / supervisor entry points ONLY — never on a plain frontend page view. Anything reading a substrate key on the frontend therefore hit an empty registry and got `RuntimeException: unknown config key '<key>'` from the fail-loud `value()` gate: a hard 500 on every logged frontend request on any site where the event logger's firehose starts (`Log_Manager::init_firehose()` reads `num_partitions`, `segment_size`, `min/max_segments`, `min/max_lifetime`). It only escaped local dev because frontend logging is off for anonymous requests there.

  `Config::is_declared()` now derives the declared set itself on first call — the substrate's own keys (Settings_Schema overlay keys ∪ config-file default keys), then the new `Config::DECLARE_ACTION` (`newspack_nodes/declare_config_keys`) so every consumer plugin declares its own. Consumers hook that action at plugin-file scope instead of pushing their keys at boot, which is what makes the keys exist by construction whenever anyone asks — the push had no safe moment: this plugin's wiring skips the frontend, and a consumer sorting alphabetically before `newspack-nodes` (event-logger-nodes) can't touch this class at its own file scope at all. `ensure_runtime_wired()` no longer declares anything.

  Two properties worth knowing: a **miss re-pulls** before it answers false, so a consumer that loads after the first read (this plugin's own file scope reads `memcache_servers` on an admin request) still gets its keys in; and the registry is **monotone** — `reset()` re-derives additively and never prunes, because a declared set that could be emptied would be hostage to every `DECLARE_ACTION` callback still being registered, turning one dropped hook into a 500 on every request. Costs nothing on the hot path: `load_config()` already builds both substrate halves on any request that reads config.

## [0.40.0] - 2026-07-13

### Changed

- **Partition/Topic/Log retention args default to `<config:*>` tokens (config-driven defaults).** An omitted retention arg on a `make_node` line — `segment_size`, `min_segments`, `max_segments`, `min_lifetime`, `max_lifetime` (Topic also `num_partitions`) — now resolves from config instead of a hardcoded `DEFAULT_*` constant. `Schema_Reflection::parse_schema_args` gained a `resolve_default()` step: a `<ns:key>` token default is run through `Core::resolve_config_tokens()` and coerced to the declared type, exactly like a positional token (which the TSL loader already resolves; a PHP schema default is not, which is why an unresolved token string previously TypeError'd the typed `int` property). Non-token defaults pass through verbatim. Caveat: a token that resolves empty (a deployment config missing the key, or the `config` namespace not yet registered) coerces to `0` and is then clamped, where a constant default was a safe fallback — the shipped `newspack-nodes-config.php` carries every retention key.

- **All one-time option migrations run on plugin activation instead of `admin_init`.** `correct_option_autoload`, `Vault_Migration`, `Remote_Settings_Migration`, and `Retention_Settings_Migration` are now all `register_activation_hook` callbacks (the migrations fire before `Bootstrap::activate`), and the `NEWSPACK_NODES_FILE` constant is dropped in favour of `__FILE__`. **Note:** activation hooks fire on (re)activation, not on an in-place plugin-file update, so an already-active install that updates without reactivating will not re-run these — the current one-time migrations already ran on existing installs under the prior `admin_init` path, so this only affects hypothetical never-activated installs.
- **`hub-control` geometry sync propagates the full `remote_*` set and re-propagates onward.** The settings-sync map now pushes `remote_min_segments` / `remote_max_lifetime` / `num_partitions` (previously missing) alongside the existing geometry keys, and additionally maps each `remote_*` key to the spoke's own `remote_*` option so a spoke forwards the geometry to ITS spokes. The substrate topology no longer syncs the `newspack_event_logger_nodes_*` performance settings — ELN ships its own shadowing `hub-control` for those.

### Fixed

- **`print_less_often()` throttles on the stable category, not the full message (faithful Tachikoma port).** `Core::print_less_often` and `Node::print_less_often` are now variadic (`$text, string ...$extra`): the rate-limiter keys on `$text` — the stable first arg — ONLY, while `$extra` is variable payload printed on the first occurrence but never folded into the key. Previously a single concatenated string was both the key and the message, so a flood of one category with differing values (`"duplicate message: expected #{$a}, got #{$b}"`) produced a fresh key every call and never throttled — inverting the intent (it logged *most* when the flood was worst). Callers now pass the stable prefix first, then the varying values as separate args (Perl's `$text, @extra`). Backward-compatible — an existing single-arg call is unchanged.
- **Swept the substrate's `print_less_often()` call sites onto the split (throttle-key vs payload) form.** Every `includes/` site that baked per-call-varying data into the single message string — exception messages, request/segment:offset positions, byte counts, dropped-message counts, handler names, transport/HTTP codes, the `<ns:key>` config token, dead-letter location/outcome, and the per-message `drop_message()` audit line (FROM/TO/payload) — now passes a stable category prefix as the first arg with the varying values as payload args. This makes those floods actually throttle to one line instead of one line per distinct value. A *bounded* failure-mode discriminator, by contrast, stays IN the key so genuinely-distinct modes still surface separately rather than collapsing to one line: the `resolve_config_token` null-vs-non-scalar-vs-unknown-namespace kind, the dead-letter `reason` enum, and each `SSE_In` error mode (buffer/event overflow, unparseable/malformed/PID-less envelope) key on their own full text. Static and per-node-stable messages (`curl_init failed`, `$this->url`, `$this->snapshot_node`, a repeating listener/event) were left unchanged. Emitted text is byte-for-byte identical.
- **Rate-limiter state simplified to a bare first-seen timestamp.** `Core::$recent_log_timers` dropped its `{timestamp, count}` shape for a plain `float` — the `count` field was written on every repeat but never read (no dump verb, no serialization, no JS mirror), so tracking it was dead work. Both writers and `prune_logs()` now store/read the timestamp directly; throttle timing is unchanged (the prune window still keys off the first-seen time).

## [0.39.0] - 2026-07-12

### Added

- **`Config::is_declared( $key )` — the registry primitive consumer accessors validate against.** Public boolean report of whether a key is in the shared registered set (schema overlay keys ∪ config-file defaults, accumulated by `register_keys()`). `Config::value()` now routes its own validation through it, and a consumer plugin's own `value()` accessor (e.g. the event-logger's, over its merged config) calls `is_declared()` to fail loud on an undeclared key without re-reading the substrate's config.
- **Fail-loud config reads: `Config::register_keys()` + `Config::value()`.** A new declarative-read layer over the substrate config. Plugins register their declared config keys; the substrate registers its own at boot in `Bootstrap::ensure_runtime_wired` as the union of the `Settings_Schema` fields (`overlay_keys()`) **and** every config-file default key (`array_keys( Config::load_config_defaults() )` — the config file is itself a declaration, so file-only keys like `vault_verify_ssl`/`vault_require_ssl` are valid reads). `Config::value( $key )` then reads a single key and throws a `\RuntimeException` for any key not in the registered set — instead of silently swallowing a renamed or typo'd key on a `?? default`. A declared key resolves to `load_config()[$key]` (option overlay or file default). The substrate's own single-key index reads (`num_partitions`, `topologies`, `memcache_servers`, `allowed_users`, `segment_size`, `min/max_segments`, `min/max_lifetime`, `vault_verify_ssl`, `vault_require_ssl` across Bootstrap, Topology_Registry, Job_Intake, Log_Cleaner, Admin, the ingest CLI, HTTP_Out, Remote_Link, and the workers/status/settings/vault service CIs) were migrated to `Config::value()`, dropping the now-redundant `?? default` / `isset` guards. Whole-array `load_config()` uses, the derived-dir token resolver, `get_base_directory()`'s own internal read, and genuinely-nested-array reads (per-topology entries, decrypted vault-server config dicts) are unchanged.

- **`list_timers` / `list_handles` in the inspector's no-node command palette.** The two Event_Framework introspection verbs (registered timers; nodes holding an EventSource/cURL-multi handle) join the no-node command buttons in the shared topology-console `Inspector`, so they're one click away in the overlay console, the hub console, and live-mode worker topologies — the fastest way to spot a drain spinner without typing.
- **`help <NodeType>` in the REPL surfaces a node's `node_schema()`.** When a `help` topic isn't a command or alias, the interpreter resolves it as a node type and renders its schema as a text block: header + category, description, `accepts_fill`/`has_target` flags, an arguments table with each argument's description, and the commands, requests, and registrations it declares. So `help Partition` documents the node's constructor arguments and verbs inline, mirroring the topology console's schema tooltips.
- **SSE glob subscriptions self-heal live.** A `{feed}.*` stream re-globs on each heartbeat and opens a Consumer for a partition dir that appears mid-stream, and removes the one whose dir vanishes (partition count increasing OR decreasing) — so a dashboard opened before a feed exists starts streaming once its first partition is created, without a reconnect. Only glob-opened readers are reconciled (exact subscriptions are never touched), and a transient `glob()` error skips the removal pass so an I/O blip can't tear down and re-tail every partition.
- **Argument tooltips in the topology console.** Constructor-argument labels (`CtorField`, shared by the Inspector's edit panel and the add-node modal) and edit-mode verb labels now surface their `node_schema` `description` as a native `title` tooltip — matching the live-mode verb tooltip, so a setting's meaning is visible while editing, not just while running. Every substrate node's constructor arguments gained a `description`, and a new `NodeSchemaCoverageTest` gate fails if any `node_schema` argument lacks one.

### Changed

- **`vault_require_ssl` now defaults to `true` (secure by default).** A remote spoke whose vault URL is not `https://` is refused — `HTTP_Out` drops the batch and `Remote_Link` refuses to open a plaintext `SSE_In`. This inverts the prior opt-in default: operators running plaintext spokes (a trusted LAN, a local dev loop) must now explicitly set `vault_require_ssl => false` (config file) or the settings-page toggle to opt back out. `vault_verify_ssl` (peer-cert verification) already defaulted `true`; the two are independent knobs.
- **`HTTP_Out` and `SSE_In` are draggable from the topology-console palette again (I/O category), and no longer need a nonce threaded through construction.** Both JS runtime nodes moved back into the `I/O` palette category (were `Remote`/`Hidden`, which the palette hides or marks non-draggable), so a fresh drop onto the canvas constructs a valid node. The request-scoped command nonce (and REST base URL) now come from the PHP-localized `window.NewspackNodesData` global at the point of use rather than from make_node arguments — a new `nodesData()` reader (`src/runtime/nodes-data.js`) plus `CommandClient.fromGlobal()`. `SseIn`'s positional schema is now just `subscribe` (`baseUrl`/`nonce` became getters that fall back to the global), so a nonce is never baked into a `.tsl`; `HttpOut` lazily defaults its `client` from the global when none was assigned. `RemoteLink`/`RemoteIpc`, which fed those coordinates through the SseIn args, are unaffected — the values they read now resolve from the same global.
- **`Log` accepts the two lifetime retention knobs too** (`min_lifetime`, `max_lifetime` — optional trailing args, default 0), giving it parity with `Partition`/`Topic`. Log already inherited Partition's dual-rule `cleanup_segments`; it just couldn't configure the age axis. Existing count-only Logs are unchanged (lifetimes default 0 = age pruning off).
- **The `dump_graph` topology envelope names a Log sink's retained-count field `max_segments`** (was the stale `num_segments`), matching the retention rename and the workers-fleet envelope. No consumer read the old key.
