- **Poison messages are dead-lettered instead of silently dropped (dead-letter [42]).** A Consumer takes an optional third arg `deadletter_dir` and builds a `:deadletter` sibling Partition there (mirrors `:offsetlog`). When a downstream node throws while processing a message, `Consumer_Node::forward_line()` quarantines the (replayable) original message to that sibling, advances past it, and emits a rate-limited alert (`Worker_Should_Stop` still propagates as control flow). With no `deadletter_dir` configured, the poison is logged and dropped. A failed quarantine write (disk full) drops-and-advances rather than re-wedging the partition. An **unparseable** source line is quarantined the same way (its raw bytes preserved for inspection) instead of being silently skipped. Replay is `wp nodes ingest <topic> <deadletter-segment>`. New `<config:deadletter_dir>` token (`{base}/deadletter`); `Topology_Registry` conflict detection now treats a shared `deadletter_dir` as a write conflict.
- **Hard-crash crawl isolates a message that kills the worker uncatchably (dead-letter [42]).** After `CRASH_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (5) respawns at one cursor with no reason stamped (an OOM/fatal/SIGKILL, not a caught throw), the Consumer enters crawl mode: it sacrifices the boot-cursor head (the in-flight-at-crash suspect) to the DLQ, then checkpoints **per message** (one line per poll) so the next uncatchable crash pins the exact in-flight offset for the following boot to quarantine. Surviving a full checkpoint interval crawling without a crash exits back to coarse mode at the healthy baseline. One accepted false-positive (the transition head). The head-sacrifice lives in the shared drain loop so the `Tail` subclass inherits it; crawl won't exit while the head is still an un-drained partial line.
- **Cooperative-stop fair-shot rule for timeout & memory stops (dead-letter [42]).** When a worker stops cooperatively (`max_runtime` or the memory watermark), the shutdown routes its durable consumers through `Consumer_Node::cooperative_stop()` instead of a blanket graceful handoff. A stop counts as a strike only when the worker stopped **while dispatching the message it booted on** — the cursor never advanced this lifetime *and* a `Worker_Should_Stop` escaped that message's `fill()`. A late "sliver" or normal memory-recycle (cursor advanced), an idle worker (empty buffer), and a message that had merely been read into the buffer but never dispatched all hand off cleanly. After `COOP_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (2) full-lifetime strikes the message is dead-lettered and the cursor advances at the virgin baseline. A memory stop whose **fresh post-reset baseline** was already near the watermark (≥ 50% of the limit) is treated as a leak / undersized `memory_limit`, not message poison: it alerts instead of striking. `Worker_Base` now categorizes each stop (`timeout`/`memory`/operational) and captures the baseline before draining. A handoff before a consumer's first poll (worker stopped on its first `should_continue`) is skipped so the 0:0 construction-default cursor can't clobber a real durable position.
- **`Tail` can quarantine poison too.** `Tail_Node` takes the optional third `deadletter_dir` arg (keeping its `source_file` naming), so a Tail's hard-crash crawl / cooperative-stop give-up routes to a `:deadletter` sibling instead of logging-and-dropping.
- **`set_line_mode` verb takes an optional `enabled` arg.** Only an explicit truthy value (`1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`, or a `<config:…>` token resolving to one) enables line mode; a bare/empty verb or any other value disables it — so the default is "off" and an accidental enable from the verb runner is reversible. The stock `job-worker.tsl` now passes `set_line_mode true` explicitly.

### Changed

- **A clean worker recycle now hands off every durable consumer at `attempts = 0`.** `Worker_Base::checkpoint_durable_consumers()` (called from both shutdown paths) graceful-checkpoints the registered work consumers *and* the IPC-input consumer, so a respawn resumes at the virgin baseline instead of mistaking the recycle for a crash. Only a hard crash skips this path, so only crashes climb the counter. The graceful checkpoint forces past the cursor-unchanged advance-guard (its `attempts = 0` is new content at the same cursor).
- **A throwing job handler is now quarantined, not silently swallowed.** `Job_Worker_Node` lets a handler exception propagate (after `after_job` runs) so the driving Consumer dead-letters the job; the stock `job-worker.tsl` wires `jobs:consumer` a `deadletter_dir`. A throwing `before_job`/`after_job` *listener* is still swallowed (app extension-point crash-protection) so it can neither take down the drain batch nor false-poison a job that actually succeeded.
- **`allow_large_writes` gains a debounced-lock mode [65].** `Partition_Node::allow_large_writes( $max_wait_ms, $debounce_ms )` — with `debounce_ms > 0` the partition no longer acquires the write lock at setup and holds it for life; instead it acquires the lock lazily on the first write of a burst and releases it after `debounce_ms` of idle (the release is debounced by the partition's own `fire()` timer). On each re-acquire it re-syncs segment state from disk, since another writer may have appended/rotated while it held nothing — so concurrent bursty writers can take turns on one partition without clobbering. `remove_node` only releases a lock it actually holds (never steals another writer's). `debounce_ms = 0` (default) keeps the original acquire-and-hold behavior; the `allow_large_writes` verb takes an optional `debounce_ms` and `dump_config` round-trips it.
- **The console persists its session state across reloads [87].** Recent transcript, command history (↑/↓ recall), `debug_level`, and the browser's `debug_state` now survive a page reload via localStorage (one namespaced module, `consolePersistence`, try/catch-guarded so private-mode/quota-full storage degrades to in-memory defaults). Transcript + history are capped to the most-recent N. `DumperNode.restore()` seeds a persisted transcript on mount.
- **The console inspector's no-node process-stats header was reworked into the per-node Activity/Throughput layout [95/98].** An **Activity** section of four peak-labeled sparkline rows (`messages in /s`, `messages out /s`, `bytes read /s`, `bytes written /s`) above a cumulative **Throughput** section (`msgs in`, `msgs out`, `bytes read`, `bytes written`), reusing the inspector's `SparklineRow`/`FieldRow`; the dmesg err/warn/dbg strip is unchanged. For a **browser** (local) graph the totals, rates, and sparklines now read the wire-accurate `IoTelemetry` counters that back the Overview tab (counted once at the SSE/HTTP boundary) so they match it exactly and avoid the `processStats` graph-rollup double-count; a **remote/worker** graph keeps the `processStats` roll-up of its `dump_metadata`, with `useAggregateRateSeries` deriving the byte read/write rate series alongside the message in/out series (clamping a worker-respawn counter reset to 0).
- **`dump_config` takes an optional regex-glob name filter (JS runtime parity with PHP).** `dump_config [ <regex glob> ]` filters the dumped nodes by name; a malformed pattern matches nothing (an empty dump), mirroring PHP `cmd_dump_config`.
- **`dump_node` now filters out references to other nodes generically (JS runtime) [96].** The inline node-state snapshot moved from `CommandInterpreterNode` into a base `Node.dumpNode()` method that excludes **any** field holding a node instance (`instanceof Node` → `'{...}'`) instead of a hardcoded name allow-list — so a composite node (e.g. `RemoteLinkNode`/`RemoteIpcNode` with their `sseIn`/`httpOut`/`heartbeat`) never leaks or circular-JSONs its internal sub-nodes, and any future composite is covered with no per-class list. The `sink` stays rendered as its name. A subclass with non-node internals (the interpreter's `_commands` verb table + `authorize` closure) overrides `dumpNode()` to mask them.

### Fixed

- **The message composer sends `send_struct` JSON without manual escaping (#32).** Composing a TM_STRUCT (or using the send_struct quick-action) previously emitted a raw `send_struct <node> <json>` line, and the console's quote-aware tokenizer (which strips quotes and has no escape) shredded the unquoted JSON into a `JSON.parse` error. The composer now wraps the JSON via a new `quoteToken()` helper (the inverse of `tokenize()`) in a quote char the value doesn't contain (prefers `'`, since JSON carries `"`), so it reaches `send_struct` as one intact token.
- **A catchable PHP fatal no longer resets the crash counter.** A fatal (OOM, uncaught error) runs `register_shutdown_function` but bypasses the cooperative `finally`; the shutdown handoff previously graceful-checkpointed (`attempts = 0`), so a message that deterministically fatals reset its counter every lifetime and never reached the hard-crash crawl. `Worker_Base::shutdown_handoff()` now detects a fatal (`error_get_last()`) and **skips** the graceful handoff, leaving the boot frame's climbing attempt count intact so the poison is eventually crawled and dead-lettered.
- **A mid-batch cooperative stop no longer rewinds the cursor over already-forwarded lines.** `Consumer_Node::drain_buffer()` performs its single cursor advance in a `finally`, so a `Worker_Should_Stop` propagating from a `pump()` mid-fill still advances past the lines already handed to the sink — they are done, and the fair-shot proxy sees the real in-flight message rather than re-delivering the batch on respawn.
- **The Consumer message counter (probe `MSGS`) counts only successfully-forwarded messages.** The increment moved to *after* a successful `sink->fill()`, so a message re-delivered after a cooperative stop, or quarantined on a throw, no longer inflates the throughput stat (it was double-counted on respawn).
- **The no-node header's rate sparklines no longer spike to the cumulative total on the first sample.** `useAggregateRateSeries` no longer seeds its baseline from a zero / not-yet-loaded reading (so the first real cumulative reading isn't `total − 0`), and it drops the baseline + history when the scope (`resetKey`) changes — so a fresh load, a shift-reload, or switching workers seeds cleanly instead of showing a one-frame totals-as-rates spike.
- **`HttpOut` now tallies `bytesRead` for the replies it receives**, mirroring its `bytesWritten` write-boundary tally, and **`RemoteLink` no longer double-counts the shared `_http` write bytes** — it surfaces its anonymous (unlisted) `SseIn`'s read tally but not the listed `_http` singleton's writes, so a graph roll-up counts each byte once.

## [0.23.0] - 2026-06-28

### Added

- **Workers log *why* they cooperatively stop.** `Worker_Base::should_continue()` now emits a `{type}.p{N}: stopping — <reason>` line (via `Core::stderr`) at every stop branch, with metrics: `lock lost` / `lock dir gone` / `restart requested` / `max_runtime exceeded (Ns / Ns)` / `memory watermark (NMB / NMB, N%)` / `db check failed N times`. Previously a `Worker_Should_Stop` exit was opaque (only a generic "stopped mid-job (pump)" at the catch). Logged once per stop (the predicate returns true until the first false ends the loop), so no volume cost.

### Changed

- **`Core::stderr` now always persists to `error_log` too, not only as a no-sink fallback.** The broadcast to the wired `_repl`/`_sse`/`_output` sink is ephemeral — it vanishes when the session ends. The default handler now also `error_log()`s every line, so worker-stop reasons (and future dead-letter alerts) survive in `debug.log` (locally) / php-errors (Atomic) even while a REPL/SSE is attached. Rate-limited callers (`Core::print_less_often`) inherit this for free.

### Fixed

- **Console Save pre-fills the *edited* topology's name, not the live console's.** Entering the editor from a live worker (e.g. `aggregator.p0`) then using Open to load a different topology (`hub-control`) left the Save dialog offering `aggregator` — it pre-filled from the live console `topology` instead of `editingName` (which Open correctly updates). Save now offers the topology you're actually editing.
- **The edit-mode inspector no longer shows the live no-node command palette.** In edit mode with nothing selected, the inspector rendered the live `_command_interpreter` header + server-command buttons (trace/dmesg/ping/…), which are meaningless for an offline draft. It now shows a "select a node / drop one from the palette" hint; selecting a node still shows the edit form.

- **Co-mounted dashboards rebuild against the FRESH backbone after Reset Graph.** A reusing mount captured its spine at mount; the owner's full rebuild (generation bump) replaces the backbone, so the reuser's next build was handed the removed `_http` / interpreter and set its client on a dead node. `runBuild` now re-syncs the spine from Core before each build.

### Changed

- **`HttpOut` packs each outbound message once instead of twice** — it already packed each message to size its write, then the client re-packed for the POST body. `postBatch` now accepts the pre-packed JSONL lines and reuses them.
- **PHP `HTTP_Out` tallies `bytes_written` / `largest_msg_sent` on POST** (JS/PHP parity): `Remote_Link::bytes_written()` reported a constant `0` because its composed `HTTP_Out` never counted the bytes it sent.
- Documented the inherent JS↔PHP `bytes_read` gap (browser `EventSource` hides SSE framing + non-`msg` events, so JS counts strictly less than PHP's full-wire tally — each is correct for what it can see; not a parity bug to "fix").

## [0.22.1] - 2026-06-28

### Changed

- **The no-node inspector gains a command palette + a `_command_interpreter` header.** When nothing is selected, the inspector now shows the interpreter identity (name + LED + live/stream status) above the process-stats header, and the quick-command buttons are relabeled lowercase with `debug` (`debug_level`), `verbose` (`debug_level 2`), and `ping` added; `trace` reflects its active state. The overlay's no-node command buttons now dispatch through the Shell's typed-line path, so shell-special verbs (`ping` → TM_PING) and local builtins (`debug_level`) work there too, not just interpreter verbs.

### Fixed

- **The hub console's "Reset Graph" chip no longer sticks on the browser graph.** The reinitNames-accumulate fix cleared it for build-delegated dashboards (the overlay), but the console is a *bare* `mountExospine()` — its per-worker RemoteIpc channels (`combined.p0`, …) never went through `runBuild`, so they weren't in `reinitNames` and `useGraphReset` counted them as user-added. `useConsoleGraph` now registers its RemoteIpc names in `reinitNames` by hand (the same exclusion the dashboards get from `runBuild`); teardown nulls `reinitNames`, so it self-cleans on rebuild.
- **Reset Graph no longer breaks the `_heartbeat → _http/workers` edge.** The heartbeat's poke target was set on RemoteLink *connect* (`ensureChildren`), so a fresh post-reset heartbeat at `/` — where the console connects no worker stream — had no target and the edge vanished. The target is fixed backbone wiring now (set in `mountBackbone`), so the edge is permanent and survives a rebuild; `ensureChildren` only arms the heartbeat's TIMER on connect.

- **The browser ADD-node modal renders constructor fields (e.g. Timer's `interval_ms`), matching the worker realm.** `useJsCatalog` copied `category`/`description`/`accepts_fill`/`has_target` from each node's `nodeSchema()` but dropped `arguments`, so a palette drop in the local (browser) realm staged an empty `argSchema` — the modal showed only `name`. The PHP class catalog (Classes_CI) already inlines `schema.arguments`; the JS catalog now does too (`schema.arguments ?? []`), so dropping a Timer offers its `interval_ms` field just like dropping into a worker topology.

- **The overlay console's no-node command buttons handle shell-special verbs (e.g. `ping`).** The overlay dispatched every button verb as a bare `TM_COMMAND` via `shell.sendCommand`, so shell-special verbs — `ping` → `TM_PING` (round-trip), `tell`/`send` → `TM_INFO`/`TM_BYTESTREAM` — arrived as `name=ping` and the interpreter rejected them ("no such verb: ping"). The overlay now parses the line through the Shell: a non-command parse result (a typed Message) is dispatched as-is, while plain interpreter verbs keep `sendCommand` — matching typed input and the hub console.

- **The console / overlay "Reset Graph" chip no longer sticks on the hub views when there's nothing to reset.** `mountExospine` overwrote `Core.reinitNames` per mount (`= builtNames`), so when several build-delegated dashboards co-mount on one page (the hub overview), only the *last* one's nodes were recognized as infra — the rest (`topicprobe:link/stream`, `topologymanager:tee/timer`, `fetch-*`, `topologymanager:in`, `workerstatus:in`) read as user-added and kept `canResetGraph` true. `runBuild` now **unions** each build's names into `reinitNames` and `teardownBuilt` drops only its own again, so every co-mounted dashboard's infra is recognized.

- **`_http` / `_heartbeat` are permanent backbone fixtures (like `_shell`), not lazily-minted RemoteLink singletons.** `mountExospine`'s `mountBackbone()` now owns them; `RemoteLink`/`RemoteIpc` and the poll dashboards (`useBatchedPoll` / `useVaultGraph` / `useDashboardGraph`) **reuse** the backbone node instead of creating their own, and teardown leaves them to the backbone. Fixes the hub console's "Reset Graph deletes `_heartbeat`/`_http` and they never come back" (the console's rebuild never re-ran a connect to recreate the lazy singletons), `cd /_http` failing after a reset, and their layout churn on return to the browser graph. The shared empty-graph/`ready` gate excludes all three backbone fixtures.

- **Browser-side nodes track byte stats too (JS parity).** The JS `Node` now exposes `bytesRead` / `bytesWritten` / `largestMsgSent` (getter/setter-backed so composites can override them); `SseIn` tallies `bytesRead` + `largestMsgSent` on each received frame, `HttpOut` tallies `bytesWritten` (packed POST size), and `RemoteLink` / `RemoteIpc` delegate those to their `SseIn` / `HttpOut` children — so `stats` and the process-stats header report real browser I/O bytes instead of `0`.

- **The aggregator's `Remote_Source` now reports real read throughput instead of 0 bytes.** `SSE_In` never tracked byte stats (only its counter), and `Remote_Link` never surfaced its children's, so a hub pulling spoke firehoses showed `0` bytes read. `SSE_In` now tracks `bytes_read` (wire bytes consumed) + `largest_msg_sent` (biggest forwarded frame), and `Remote_Link` (so `Remote_Source` / `Remote_Ipc`) delegates `counter()` / `bytes_read()` / `largest_msg_sent()` to its `SSE_In` child and `bytes_written()` to its `HTTP_Out` child — the same composite-aggregation pattern `Topic` uses over its `Partition`s.

- **The console process-stats header's In/Out rate sparklines no longer reset when you select a node or collapse the inspector.** The rate series accumulated inside the no-node header component, which unmounts on either action — wiping the history. It now accumulates in the always-mounted `GraphView` (`useAggregateRateSeries`) and is passed to the header as a prop, so it persists and keeps ticking while the header is hidden.

### Changed

- **The inspector's Compose and Register modals use the standard `topology-modal__*` field classes** (`__body` / `__label` / `__input` / `__actions`), matching the other modals so the shared modal theming applies uniformly.

## [0.22.0] - 2026-06-27

### Added

- **Process-stats header in the console inspector** (roadmap [95]). The no-node inspector leads with vitals for the process being viewed (whatever `_cwd` points at): **messages in** (source-node counters — `has_target`, `!accepts_fill`), **messages out** (sink-node counters — `!has_target`, `accepts_fill`), **bytes read**, and **bytes written** rolled up from the live `dump_metadata` graph; **In/Out rate sparklines** derived from successive `dump_metadata` polls (`useAggregateRateSeries`); and **error / warning / debug counts** from a `dmesg` of that process — the new `_dmesg` poll node classifies the stderr tail (`WARNING:`/`ERROR:`/else) and publishes the counts.

- **Message-composer playground** (roadmap [46]). The no-node inspector gains a **Compose** button opening a modal to build a message from scratch — pick a target node, a message TYPE (`TM_BYTESTREAM`/`TM_INFO`/`TM_STRUCT`/`TM_REQUEST`/`TM_EOF`), and a value — dispatched via the matching CLI verb (`send_node` / `tell_node` / `send_struct` / `request_node` / `send_eof`), so it's fully equivalent to typing the command at the REPL.

- **Topology drift diff** (roadmap [49]). The console marks runtime **drift** — live nodes in the running graph but NOT in the topology's registered `.tsl` (added at runtime via the console / `make_node`) — with a distinct brass dashed outline, so temporary/unregistered nodes stand apart from the canonical graph. Reserved `_` console infra and patron sidecars (already hidden) are excluded; live mode only.

- **The selected-node inspector can register/unregister listeners** (roadmap [48], part C). A **Register** button (shown when the node's class declares registration events) opens a modal to wire a listener node to one of the node's valid events — dispatching `register <source> <target> <event>`. Current registrations render as an `event → listener` list, each with an × that dispatches `unregister`.

- **The selected-node inspector gains Request, EOF, Tell, and Struct action buttons** — `request_node` / `send_eof` (direct), and `tell_node` / `send_struct` via a shared value-prompt modal (one `PromptModal` keyed by verb). (roadmap [48], part 2)

- **The no-node inspector is a server-command palette** — Trace (`debug_state *`), `dmesg`, `dump_config`, `dump_metadata`, `stats` — each dispatching its command via the inspector's generic `command` action (a one-click alternative to typing them at the REPL prompt). (roadmap [48], part 1)

- **Idle nodes are dimmed in the graph.** A node whose message rate is below the display floor (no meaningful activity) renders at reduced opacity — like a quiet connection — so active nodes stand out. Live mode only; edit mode (no rate data) never dims, and a hover-fade still takes precedence. (roadmap [85])

- **The overlay Overview shows Client Uptime and SSE Uptime cards.** Client uptime is time since the page loaded (`performance.timeOrigin`); SSE uptime is time since the live stream connected — `SseInNode` stamps the connect time into `IoTelemetry` on CONNECTED and clears it on DISCONNECTED/RECONNECTING, so the card reads `-` while down. Both format as an age and tick with the cards' existing refresh (no new timer). (roadmap [89])

- **The topicprobe record now carries the offsetlog cache size** — `Probe_Record::CACHE_SIZE` (index 9) is the byte size of the consumer's newest offsetlog segment, set from `Consumer::probe_stats()` (0 for ephemeral readers). Mirrored in `probe-record.js` with the PHP↔JS parity test extended. The hub overview graphs it as a **Topics Cache Size** panel (alongside Message Rate / Byte Rate / Backlog), and the SummaryCards row shows **Avg Cache** + **Total Cache** cards. (roadmap [89])

- **The debug overlay is back on the hub Console tab** — it now rides every hub tab, so you can watch a worker (the Console) and this browser's own nodes/I/O (the overlay's Overview) at once. On the Console tab the overlay runs **Overview-only**: its graph+REPL would duplicate the Console's and collide on the shared `_output` infra, so the Inspector body builds no infra there (`buildRepl=false`) and points back at the Console. A `key`-free re-render with the existing cleanup-before-effect ordering keeps the tab-switch collision-free (guarded by `DevToolsHub.outputCollision.test`).

- **`dump_config` now accepts an optional regex glob** that filters the dump to nodes whose name matches it — Tachikoma parity (`dump_config [<regex glob>]`). No argument dumps the whole graph as before. The node inspector also gains a **Config** button (beside Dump) that runs `dump_config <node>` for the selected node. `dump_config` also omits patron-managed sidecars (a Consumer's `:source` / `:offsetlog`) — their patron's own config line recreates them, so dumping them separately would duplicate them on replay (both the PHP and JS interpreters).

- **The inspector now shows a read-only Constructor section for the selected live node.** It mirrors edit mode's constructor form but read-only: it pairs the class's declared positional argument names (from the catalog schema) with the values the node was given — its `arguments` string, already carried in every node's `dump_metadata` row. An omitted optional argument falls back to its schema default (shown dimmed). To change a node's arguments, delete and recreate it (there is no live re-arg). A free-form trailing argument folds into its declared slot instead of spilling across rows, and a class with no constructor arguments (or a reserved node) shows no section.

### Changed

- **Dropping a node in live mode now shows the class's node_schema Constructor fields** instead of one freeform "arguments" string — the same per-field `CtorField` widgets edit mode uses (typed text, formatter/node-name pickers, per-field defaults shown as placeholders). On confirm the per-field values serialize to the `make_node` args exactly as edit-mode `serializeTsl` does (defaults filled, trailing empties dropped). `CtorField` / `coerceValue` / `inputForType` were extracted to a shared `components/CtorField.js` module consumed by both the Inspector and the modal.

### Fixed

- **The edit inspector hides node_schema verbs flagged `hidden`.** Tail's time-travel verbs (`set_snapshot_node`, `seek_frame`, `pause`, `play`, `step`, …) are schema plumbing, not operator-facing config — they no longer clutter the editor's Verbs list, matching the runtime action-button filter.

- **Selecting a node no longer steals keyboard focus into the REPL transcript.** With the transcript open, clicking a node refocused the REPL input — and the document-level Delete/Backspace handler skips form fields — so you couldn't delete a node without first minimizing the transcript. Selection now leaves focus alone.

- **Every modal now has an X close button, and the Register/Compose modals gained a Cancel button.** `ModalShell` renders a close (×) affordance in the header corner, so all dialogs (Confirm/Prompt/NewNode/Register/Compose) can be dismissed without ESC or a backdrop click. The inspector's Register and Compose modals — which previously had only a primary action (on a button that was even missing its base style class) — now match the others with a Cancel button.

- **Vault commands are now observable via `connect _shell`.** The Vault's CRUD/Test dispatches entered straight at the interpreter, bypassing the `_shell` command Tap — so there was no way to see what the Test buttons sent or when. They now route through `_shell` (→ interpreter → the named `_http`/HttpOut egress), like every other command path.

- **No-node inspector command buttons now pass their arguments.** The generic `command` action split off the verb but dispatched with empty args, so `Trace` (`debug_state *`) arrived as a bare `debug_state` — toggling only the interpreter (`_command_interpreter debug_state: 1`) instead of every node. It now forwards the args after the verb (`*`).

- **Console deep links (`?topology=<name>`) now open the requested topology instead of the first one.** The initial topology pick validated the URL param against a render-time re-read of `window.NewspackNodesData.topologyWorkers` — but each hub bundle (event-dashboards, devtools-hub, console, …) localizes its OWN `NewspackNodesData` global, and the last to execute clobbered `topologyWorkers`, so the live read saw `{}` and EVERY deep link fell back to the first topology. It now validates against the module-load snapshot (`SEED_PARTITIONS`, the same source as the dropdown), falling back to the live read only when the snapshot was empty at import.

- **The `>= 1000` router-hitchhike no longer kills the router's own tick, and the JS timer now matches it.** The `>= 1000` threshold (previous release, PHP only) made the `_router` hitchhike its OWN per-tick TIMER — registering on itself, never entering the event framework, so it never ticked and every hitchhiking timer (probes, heartbeats, supervisor cadence, log pruning) silently died; tests that drive `fire_cb()` directly masked it. `set_timer()` now exempts the router so it always owns a slot — PHP guards by identity (`$router !== $this`), the JS `TimerNode` by an `isRouter` flag (the JS router self-arms in its constructor before it's named). The same `>= 1000` threshold + guard now applies to the JS `TimerNode`/`RouterNode`, so both runtimes match.

- **A worker's first `dump_metadata` reading no longer spikes the per-node message/byte rates.** The node-detail ACTIVITY sparklines (messages/s, bytes read/s) are deltas between polls. A node enters the graph at `count: 0` (a structural placeholder) and the first `dump_metadata` backfills the FULL cumulative counter at once — a worker that has run for minutes reports e.g. 12k messages / 2.3 MB in ONE response — so the next sample divided ~12k by a single poll interval, producing a bogus `peak 10569 /s` / `peak 2.0 M/s` that poisoned the auto-scaled peak label. `useGraphRates` now keeps a node "cold" (rate 0, no history) until its first reading WITH data seeds the baseline; real per-interval rates accrue only from the sample after, so the cumulative backfill never becomes a rate.

- **Console modals (`ModalShell`) now portal to `<body>` so they can't be sliced by the header.** A modal raised from a nested stacking context — e.g. the Inspector's send-bytes `PromptModal`, rendered inside the inspector dock's `z-index: 2` console — paints *below* the panel header (the header was portaled up so the hub edit-mode settings modal could anchor to the settings button). A `position: fixed` backdrop's `z-index` only competes inside its own stacking context, so the `NEWSPACK::NODES` header sliced through the middle of the modal (title above, input hidden, buttons below). `ModalShell` now renders through a `createPortal` to `document.body` inside a `display: contents` `theme-<slug>` wrapper (skin tokens stay in scope, no layout box), escaping every nested context. The `position: fixed` full-viewport backdrop dims the whole page and its `z-index` (1000000) clears the overlay panel (999998) — replacing the old `.nodes-debug`-scoped backdrop lift, which the portal had escaped down to the `9000` default (leaving the modal painted *under* the canvas). The dialog itself is then positioned at the overlay panel's centre (measured from `.nodes-debug__panel`), so it reads as centered *in the overlay* rather than the viewport; the standalone console (no panel) falls back to viewport-centering. Palette-drop `NewNodeModal` was already root-rendered and unaffected.

- **The `_shell` console Tap no longer shows in the overlay console's PATH menu.** The debug overlay listed every `_`-prefixed node not in its non-navigable set as a `cd` target, so `_shell` — the observe-only **routing** Tap `useBatchedPoll` mounts in front of `_http` on every dashboard (commands route `_shell/_http/<ci>`) — appeared alongside `/` and `/_http`. It's send-path plumbing, not a navigable scope, so it's excluded now (`names.CONSOLE_TAP` added to the menu's non-navigable set); `_http`, the I/O egress, stays a `cd` target. Also corrected a `useBatchedPoll` comment that filed `_shell` under "I/O-boundary node names" — it's a routing Tap, not an I/O node.

### Changed

- **`debug_state *` reports every node it set** (PHP + JS parity). Instead of a single `* debug_state: N`, it prints a `Setting all nodes to debug_state: N` header followed by one `<node> debug_state: N` line per node (sorted) — so a bulk trace toggle is auditable, not opaque.

- **`_shell` is now a permanent fixture of the exospine backbone.** `mountExospine` always mounts the `_shell` command Tap in front of `_command_interpreter`; every constructed Shell and the dashboards' periodic poll commands route through it, so `connect _shell` observes ALL outbound commands consistently (with or without a REPL). Removed the per-consumer `_shell` creation (console, `useBatchedPoll`, debug overlay), which now bind to the shared one. Unlike the rest of the rule-#2 backbone, `_shell` is **visible** in the canvas (it's the command-observation point) — but it's excluded from the empty-graph / "ready" check since it's always present.

- **Renamed the per-topology worker-count snapshot `topologyPartitions` → `topologyWorkers`** (the `NewspackNodesData` localize key + its PHP/JS identifiers). Each entry is a topology's worker count, so "partition" overloaded the term (it already means log partitions / `Partition_Node`). The partition *index* of a worker (`p0`/`p1`, `partitionIndices`) keeps the partition term — that's a worker's actual partition number.

- **The debug overlay's "Messages" heading is themed** — small uppercase muted label matching the stat-card labels, instead of the browser-default serif `h3` that read as unstyled.

- **Valid registration events are now declared in `node_schema()`** (Tachikoma-style, single source), in **both PHP and JS**. `Timer` declares `FIRE`, `Topic` `READY`, `Router` `FIRE`+`TIMER`+`NOT_AVAILABLE` in `node_schema()['registrations']` / `nodeSchema().registrations`; the base node constructor's `seed_registrations()` / `seedRegistrations()` turns that into the runtime allow-list, and `register()` still rejects undeclared events ("no such event"). Replaces the per-node hand-seeding of `registrations`, and makes the events introspectable via the class catalog (`classes list` now carries each class's `registrations`) for the upcoming register/unregister UI. (roadmap [48], part C)

- **"+ New Topology" moved to the hub header** (upper-right), matching the Vault tab's "+ Add Server". The Overview portals it into the shared header-controls slot (`createPortal`) instead of trailing the SummaryCards row; standalone (no hub slot) it renders inline.

- **`help` lists one unified `### COMMANDS ###` section** instead of separate SHELL BUILTINS / SERVER COMMANDS sections — the shell builtins (`cd`, `debug_level`, `tell`, `send`, `send_struct`, `send_eof`, `request`, `ping`, `status`, `show_parse`) are folded into the single per-command help table (PHP `$H` + JS `HELP`), so `help` and tab-completion cover them uniformly.

- **The supervisor restart button matches the topology restart buttons.** The hub-overview supervisor row's restart button now uses the same `nodes-ctl__restart button button-small` classes as the topology rows (WP small-button box + amber ↻) instead of a one-off `nodes-tm__restart` style, so the two share one look. The orphaned `.nodes-tm__restart` rule is removed. (roadmap [90])

- **`node_schema()` command handlers are now named `cmd_*` methods, not inline closures.** Every node's schema stays declarative — it links a named handler via a thin arrow-fn (`'handler' => static fn ( … ) => self::cmd_x( … )`) instead of embedding the body — matching the JS `CommandInterpreter` verb-table pattern. Covers all 12 PHP nodes that carried inline handlers (the service CIs, `Partition`, `Consumer`, `Settings_Sync`); the JS runtime already used named methods. Behavior-preserving — verb tests verify each. (roadmap [94])

- **Patron-managed sidecars no longer create their own `{name}:config` interpreter.** A sidecar (a Partition/Consumer that has a patron — e.g. a Consumer's `:source` / `:offsetlog`) is configured directly by its patron and is already excluded from `dump_config`, so the ctor-auto-wired `:config` interpreter was an unused node. `Node::patron()` now drops it when a patron is set; standalone Partitions keep their `:config`. (roadmap [83])

- **The browser SSE receive node and the PHP `SSE_In` now share one shape and aligned reporting.** `sse-connector-node.js` folded into `sse-in-node.js` (one `SseInNode extends Node`); the substrate's `connected` handshake travels as a flat `PID … SLOT … SUBSCRIPTIONS … INTERVAL …` string (TM_INFO values are strings, never arrays), parsed into plain `sessionPid`/`sessionSlot` exposed via `pid()`/`slot()` on both sides; the vestigial `partition` field is gone end-to-end (the slot pool keys on user/ip/slot). Every error path on both sides now logs an `ERROR:`-prefixed line (`ERROR: disconnected - …` / `ERROR: reconnecting - …`) alongside a semantic `set_state`, and PHP's transient `INIT` folded into `CONNECTING` for 5-state parity. A `connected` handshake missing its PID is reported (ERROR) and not marked connected on both runtimes.

- **A 1000 ms `Timer_Node` now router-hitchhikes instead of claiming its own event-framework slot.** `set_timer()`'s threshold moved from `$ms > 1000` to `$ms >= 1000`: an exactly-1000 ms interval is now paced by the ~1 s router tick (the boundary case where the per-second tick is enough) rather than registering a dedicated sub-second slot. Only `$ms < 1000` still claims its own slot.

- **Renamed the shared `SliceViewNode` file to kebab-case** for node-file naming consistency: `@newspack-nodes/shared/nodes/SliceViewNode` → `@newspack-nodes/shared/nodes/slice-view-node`. The exported class `SliceViewNode` is unchanged; every other node-class file in the tree is already kebab (`*-view-node.js`), so the shared base now matches. Adopters importing the base must update the path: `import { SliceViewNode } from '@newspack-nodes/shared/nodes/slice-view-node'`.

## [0.21.0] - 2026-06-27

### Added

- **Theme-storage helpers moved to `@newspack-nodes/shared/theme` so sibling plugins can read the console-selected skin.** `getStoredTheme`, `THEME_STORAGE_KEY`, `DEFAULT_THEME`, `THEMES`, and `isValidTheme` move from `src/topology-console/themes.js` to a new `src/shared/theme.js`; `themes.js` re-exports them (every console importer unchanged) and keeps only its console-only palette/inspector collapse keys. Lets a standalone consumer page (e.g. an ELN dashboard) read the persisted skin and apply the theme token-context without reaching into topology-console internals.

- **The Raw Logs and Topic Probe SSE dashboards now route their stream through a named pass-through `Tee`** (`rawlogs:stream`, `topicprobe:stream`) on the edge between the stream source and its view, so the live stream can be watched via `connect <tee>` in the debug overlay without disturbing the dashboard. The Tee has a single target (the view), so the view receives exactly what it did before.
- **`SliceViewNode` promoted to `@newspack-nodes/shared/nodes/SliceViewNode` — the shared thin-view-node base every dashboard rebuild's slice views extend.** The thin per-widget view node that owns ONE slice of a model (parse its own command reply's JSON-string `VALUE.payload`, publish via `setState('view', …)`; a `TM_ERROR` reply — string OR `{ message }` payload — surfaces as `{ ...emptySlice(), error }`; an unparseable payload keeps the prior slice so transient garbage never blanks the widget; subclasses supply only `emptySlice()`) lived only in the bundled example (`examples/example-ai-newsletter/src/dashboard/nodes/slice-view-node.js`). It moves to the canonical shared tree so every future dashboard's view nodes extend one base instead of re-copying it. Added an OPTIONAL `PendingReplies` settle path: a subclass that ALSO awaits a verb (a future vault test, a topology mutate, a hook-catalog modal) assigns `this.replies = new PendingReplies()`, and `fill()` settles a matching reply first (returning early when `this.replies.settle(message)` matches) before the slice path; with no pending match — or no `replies` at all — the node behaves exactly as before. The example's three view nodes (`source-counts`/`top-table`/`accumulated`) now import the base from `@newspack-nodes/shared/nodes/SliceViewNode`; the local base file and its test are removed, the test folding into the new shared `src/shared/nodes/__tests__/SliceViewNode.test.js`.
- **`Partition_Node::read_latest_snapshot_cache( $offsets_dir, $glob, $cache_key = 'cache', $items_key = 'items' ): array` — the reusable offsetlog-snapshot glob+flatten read.** Globs `$offsets_dir/$glob` (`GLOB_ONLYDIR`), reads each matched dir's newest committed record via the existing `read_latest_value_at()`, descends `VALUE[$cache_key][$items_key]`, and concatenates the array-shaped items into one flat list — the per-dir glob + cache-descent dance a Service_CI doing partitioned-snapshot reads used to hand-roll, lifted to a substrate primitive (callers memoize per request; this re-globs each call). Fault-tolerant per dir: a missing/non-array cache, non-array items list, or non-array item is silently skipped; no matches → `[]`. The example AI-newsletter's `Insights_CI_Demo_Node::read_snapshot_items()` is now a one-liner over this (pinning only its `example-scored.p*` glob), dropping its private `read_cache_items()`.
- **`Service_CI_Node::slice_verb( callable $shape ): \Closure` — the slice-verb builder.** A `protected static` helper that turns a shape closure (`function ( Command_Interpreter_Node $ci ): mixed` — the interpreter IS the CI for a Service_CI verb) into a verb handler matching the `( Command_Interpreter_Node, string, array )` signature that passes the CI to `$shape` and `wp_json_encode`s the result. Lets a CI's read-only slice verbs be 2–3 lines sharing one memoized read instead of each repeating the json-encode dance, and other CIs (the upcoming Performance_CI decomposition) reuse it. Authorization stays central — `commands_from_schema()` wraps every handler with `require_manage_options()`, so the slice handler never self-gates. The example's three `Insights_CI_Demo_Node` slice verbs (`counts`/`top`/`accumulated`) now build their handlers with it, dropping the per-class `$slice` factory.
- **Shared dashboard SCSS modules `@newspack-nodes/shared/styles/{tokens,mixins,components}` — the design-token / mixin / shared-class set every dashboard `base.scss` re-declared verbatim, extracted to one source.** Pure dedup, no token-vocabulary change: `_tokens.scss` (the `$term-*`/`$dark-*`/`$light-*`/`$status-*` vars), `_mixins.scss` (the ~20 chrome/table/control mixins), and `_components.scss` (the shared `.newspack-nodes-*` classes, `.entry-*` log rows, and `@keyframes skeleton-pulse`). The build-kit `scssPlugin` now threads the consumer's esbuild `alias` map into a Sass `findFileUrl` importer so SCSS `@use`/`@forward` can pull these partials through the `@newspack-nodes/*` surface (previously the alias resolved for JS imports only). `src/event-dashboards/styles/base.scss` is migrated as the proof: it now `@forward`s the tokens + mixins (so siblings keep resolving `base.$dark-text`, `@include base.dark-search-input`, …) and `@use`s the shared components — the compiled `event-dashboards` CSS is byte-identical before vs after. The other four dashboard `base.scss` files (in `newspack-event-logger-nodes`) are deliberately a follow-on, pending the `--np-*`-vs-universal theming decision.
- **`useBatchedPoll(opts)` + `addSliceFetcher(interpreter, slice)` — the dashboard batched-poll toolkit (`@newspack-nodes/shared`).** The two helpers that lift the poll-pattern dashboard boilerplate the example used to hand-wire. `useBatchedPoll` (a React hook — page-visibility needs React; `src/shared/hooks/useBatchedPoll.js`) owns the entire mount/batch skeleton: it `mountExospine`s the backbone, pre-creates the `_shell` Tap + `_http` HttpOut (with an injectable `commandClient` test seam), creates a fan-out `Tee` (`teeName`) + a router-hitchhike `Timer` (`timerName`) that fans each tick to it, brackets the router TIMER tick with `http.lock()` / `http.flush()` so a tick's commands batch into ONE POST, and gates the Timer on page visibility (HIDDEN unregisters it from the router TIMER → no POST; VISIBLE re-registers). The caller passes a `build( { interpreter, tee } )` that adds only its dashboard-specific nodes and the egress target path `_shell/_http/<ci>`; it returns `{ interpreterRef }` and re-renders after each build (the `bumpBuild` semantics) so widgets' `useNodeState` re-subscribe to the freshly-mounted view nodes. `addSliceFetcher` (a pure function; `src/shared/helpers/addSliceFetcher.js`) is the per-slice `SLICES.forEach` body as one call: it wires `makeNode('Fetcher', fetcher, '<receiver> <command>')` → `connectNode(target)`, fans the supplied Tee to it, creates the receiver `Tee` connected to the view node, makes the view node, and (optional) inserts a `transform: { name, nodeClass, args }` node on the receiver-Tee → view edge so a per-slice merge/dedup lands on a graph edge instead of inside the view; it returns the receiver name.
- **`Fetcher` JS runtime node (`Control` category).** A reusable dashboard-composition primitive that turns ANY trigger message into ONE configured command send — the building block for `Timer → Tee → Fetchers → _shell/_http/<ci>` graphs where the Timer tick hitchhikes every fetcher's command into one HTTP POST. `arguments = <receiver> <command> [<command_args>...]` (Tachikoma positional style, parsed in the `arguments` setter): `receiver` is the local node the server's reply routes back TO (stamped as the emitted command's `FROM`), `command` is the verb, and the joined remainder is the command arguments. `fill( message )` IGNORES the trigger payload — every message is just a trigger — and emits ONE `TM_COMMAND` whose `FROM` = the configured receiver and `VALUE = { name: <command>, arguments: <command_args> }`, forwarded through `sink` with `TO` stamped from `target` by the base `fill()` (the dashboard `connect_node`s the Fetcher's target to `_shell`/`_http`/`<ci>`; the node itself hardcodes no path). The command is configured on the node, never read from the message (a node that sends the command carried in its message is a Shell). Registered as `Fetcher` in `CommandInterpreterNode.includeNodes`, so `makeNode( 'Fetcher', name )` resolves it.
- **`wp nodes activate <topology>` / `wp nodes deactivate <topology>` CLI verbs.** A headless path to activate (add to the persisted active set + spawn the fleet now) and deactivate (remove + drain) a topology — closing the gap where the only way to toggle a topology was the Settings → Topologies UI (and `wp nodes restart` rejects a not-yet-spawned type). `activate` validates the name against the catalog (`Topology_Registry::describe()`), erroring with the available catalog names on a miss, is idempotent (already-active re-spawns, no duplicate), and refuses a write-conflict before persisting. The option-write + cache-invalidate + spawn/drain logic is extracted onto the shared `Topology_Registry::activate()` / `Topology_Registry::deactivate()` primitives, which the existing `Topologies_CI_Node` REST/UI verbs now also call (the inline closures were de-duplicated onto them).
- **Generic `Node::dump_metadata(): array` hook.** A per-node seam to contribute extra fields into its `dump_metadata` row; the base returns `[]`. `cmd_dump_metadata()` merges it with `+=` (the fixed metadata keys always win — the hook can only add), so the interpreter stays generic with no per-subclass special-casing.
- **Time-travel transport verbs on `Consumer_Node` (base, so `Tail` and every consumer inherit them).** Back a debugger UI that pauses a consumer, seeks it to an offsetlog keyframe, and single-steps it message-by-message. The READ surface (the offsetlog keyframe list + the live cursor) rides `dump_metadata` via `dump_metadata()` — see "Changed" below. Auth-gated commands (`{name}:config` verbs — the TM_REQUEST path bypasses `interpret()`'s auth gate, so every MUTATING verb is a command): `STEP` implies PAUSE (stops the self-rearming `fire()` loop so it can't interleave full-batch polls between steps), forces one-message granularity, emits at most one message, advances the durable cursor, and replies with the `{ seg, off, at_eof }` cursor as JSON; `SEEK_FRAME <segment_id>` reads that ONE offsetlog segment (its id comes from `dump_metadata`'s `frames[].id`), `restore_state()`s its co-committed `cache` into the snapshot node, and repositions the read cursor to the record's SOURCE `{seg,off}` (stays paused — does not re-arm the timer); `PAUSE` stops the poll timer; `PLAY` restores the line_mode `STEP` captured (not hardcoded false — `line_mode` is a legitimate production setting) and re-arms the `fire()` loop. New `Consumer_Node::$saved_line_mode` holds the pre-STEP mode for the session.
- **Time-travel PLAY truncate-on-resume + `Partition_Node::truncate_after( int $segment_id )`.** A rewind seek among offsetlog keyframes stays non-destructive while paused (STEP/PAUSE don't checkpoint), but on `PLAY` — the commit-to-this-branch moment — a rewound `Consumer_Node` now truncates its offsetlog before re-arming the timer, so the re-written forward timeline stays monotonic instead of going out of sync (a new frame at the highest id but with a SOURCE cursor behind the retained later frames). `seek_frame()` records the rewind point in the new private `Consumer_Node::$rewound_to`; `play()` calls `$this->offsetlog?->truncate_after( $this->rewound_to )` then clears it (a normal pause→play with no prior seek leaves `rewound_to` null → no truncation; a second seek overwrites it with the newer branch point). The new substrate primitive `Partition_Node::truncate_after()` deletes (unlinks) every segment with id > `$segment_id`, then resets the write state so the log continues coherently FROM `$segment_id` (`current_segment_id`/`current_size` reset to that segment, the cached file handle is closed, and `segments_cache` becomes the survivor list maintaining the rotation-cache invariant) — the next checkpoint rotates cleanly to `$segment_id + 1` (monotonic, no gap, no survivor overwritten). No-op when `$segment_id` is the newest, past the newest, or absent. The OFFSETLOG only — never the source log: `truncate_after()` is single-writer only, so it throws a `\RuntimeException` (mirroring `allow_large_writes()`'s fail-loud contract) when the partition holds an exclusivity `write_lock` (an `allow_large_writes()`-locked, multi-writer-guarded source) — the consumer's lock-free `void_warranty()` offsetlog passes the guard.
- **The `Consumer_Node` offsetlog is now an exact keyframe timeline for time-travel** — `OFFSETLOG_SEGMENT_SIZE` 65536→**1** and `OFFSETLOG_NUM_SEGMENTS` 2→**10**. `Partition_Node::do_rotate()` adopts the still-empty newest segment on the first commit and rotates to a fresh segment on every commit after (so `segment_size=1` produces no empty-segment spam), making **one checkpoint = one segment = one frame** uniformly for stateless (small offset records) and stateful/snapshot (offset + cache) consumers. `num_segments=10` retains the last 10 keyframes; `load_offsetlog()` crash-resume still reads the newest segment (now exactly one record). The keyframe list in `dump_metadata`'s `frames` IS this segment list, so each frame's id is its offsetlog segment id.
- **`newspack_nodes/devtools_overlay_pages` filter + `Admin::devtools_overlay_pages()`.** The shared registry of admin page slugs (besides the hub) that embed `<DebugOverlay>`. An overlay-tab-providing bundle (e.g. ELN's `current-request` "Request" tab) enqueues its tab on these pages, so a consumer plugin gets the full overlay tab set just by declaring its page on the filter — not only the hub and the tab provider's own pages. The substrate's own hub-host tab bundles still enqueue only on the hub, so consumer pages don't pull in the hub dashboards.
- **Universal `--chart-1..8` categorical-series tokens and `--{oxide,sage,brass,cyan}-subtle` tint tokens** in the hub theme vocabulary. Defined once in the ROOT `.topology-app` block as `color-mix`/`var()` derivations of each theme's own accents (`--cyan`/`--sage`/`--brass`/`--oxide` + their `-dark` shades), so chart series and status tints re-skin per theme with no per-theme-block edits; the `theme-newspack` skin maps `--chart-1..6` onto the sanctioned `--np-chart-*` brand palette.
- **General `'hidden' => true` flag on a node command schema** keeps a `:config` verb out of the topology-console inspector's generic per-command verb-button list. The four `Consumer_Node` time-travel verbs (`SEEK_FRAME`, `PAUSE`, `PLAY`, `STEP`) carry it because they are already driven by the inspector's Time Travel transport bar — the standalone buttons were redundant. Declarative, not a hardcoded name list in the JS: `Classes_CI_Node::strip_commands()` carries the flag through the catalog (default-omitted when false/absent, like `multiple`), and the inspector filters out any command whose `hidden` is truthy. The Time Travel panel is unaffected (it builds its own invoke transport bar). Non-transport config verbs (`set_snapshot_node`, `set_line_mode`, …) stay visible.
- **`Consumer_Node` exposes its poll state as a `polling` signal in `dump_metadata` (`INIT` | `ACTIVE` | `PAUSED`), and the topology console consumes it.** `arguments()`/`play()` set `ACTIVE`, `pause()` and now `step()` set `PAUSED` (via `set_state('POLLING', …)`); `dump_metadata()` reports it as `polling` (default `INIT`). `step()` previously stopped its timer — leaving the consumer genuinely paused — but never updated the signal, so a direct STEP left `polling` stale at `ACTIVE`; it now sets `PAUSED` consistent with `pause()`. The console threads the field onto the node (`parseMetadata`, present-only) and uses it as the source of truth for the Time Travel transport: the Inspector passes `paused={ 'PAUSED' === node.polling }` to `TimeTravelPanel`, which syncs the gate to the signal with an **optimistic override** (a PAUSE/PLAY click flips the gate instantly for feedback, then the next metadata signal reconciles it). The graph canvas shows a ⏸ badge (tokenized `--brass`) on the card of any node whose `polling === 'PAUSED'`, so a held consumer is visible without selecting it.
- **`Consumer_Node` reports its cursor POSITION as `at_frame` + `on_frame` in `dump_metadata`, describing where the cursor sits relative to the offsetlog keyframes for BOTH live status and time-travel — so a quiet live consumer reads "on frame N" and the topology console's Time Travel panel survives a remount.** A single pair replaces the prior `parked_frame`/`stepped`. `at_frame` (int|null) is the keyframe the cursor is at-or-just-past — its current checkpoint: `$this->rewound_to` when seeked, else the NEWEST offsetlog frame id when live (the cursor reads forward from its last checkpoint), null only when there are no frames yet. `on_frame` (bool) is whether the cursor sits exactly on `at_frame`'s committed position vs has advanced past it — seeked it's `! stepped_since_seek`, live it's `cursor == last checkpoint` (a QUIET consumer sits ON its last checkpoint; an actively-reading one is past it). Because `at_frame` tracks the newest frame while live, the panel now reads a quiet live consumer as "**on frame N**" instead of the old "live — after frame N". The private `$stepped_since_seek` flag (set by `step()`, cleared by `seek_frame()`/`play()`) is retained to feed `on_frame`'s seeked case. `parseMetadata` threads `at_frame`/`on_frame` onto the node present-only (`'at_frame' in meta`, since null is meaningful), the Inspector passes them to `TimeTravelPanel` as `atFrameSignal` / `onFrameSignal` (alongside `paused`), and the panel SEEDS `atFrame` / `onFrame` from those signals on mount and RECONCILES them on each signal change — mirroring the existing `paused` optimistic-override pattern. Rewind snaps onto `at_frame` when off it, else steps to the previous keyframe; fast-forward seeks the next; the position label reads "on frame N" / "between frame N and M" (paused) / "after frame N" (live, reading ahead); follow-head falls out for free (live ⇒ `at_frame` = newest each poll). Transport clicks still drive the position optimistically; the next poll's signal reconciles.
- **Read-only "Effective Configuration" panel on the Nodes Runtime settings page.** Below the settings form, a `widefat` table now reports, per substrate setting: the stored option value (or "— (file default)" when unset), the value the next worker will load (overlay-resolved `Config::load_config()`), any active `Options_Overlay` override, and the live restart impact — "Applies on next supervisor tick" for `supervisor_only`, "Takes effect immediately" for no-restart fields, or "Restarts: <topologies>" (resolved through `Restart_Planner::topologies_for()` against the live topology graphs; "Restarts: (no active consumer)" when the classification matches no active topology). `Admin::render_effective_config_section()` (hooked to `newspack_nodes/settings_after_form`) renders it. Large array-valued settings (e.g. an event-logger hook list with hundreds of entries) are summarized as a count + first-6 sample (`"<n> values: a, b, … (+<rest> more)"`) so they can't dominate the row; small arrays (≤6) render in full and an empty array shows "(none)". An associative-array setting (e.g. `custom_events` `{event => true}`) shows its keys, not the `true`→`1` values.

### Changed

- **`Command_Interpreter_Node::resolve_class()` is memoized.** It loops the registered namespace prefixes doing `class_exists` + `new ReflectionClass(...)->isAbstract()` per candidate, and `Restart_Planner` calls it once per graph node per active topology — re-resolving the same handful of types (`Partition`, `Topic`, `Log`, …) every time. It now caches **successes only** (type → FQCN) in a static map; misses are NOT cached, so a type resolvable only after a later `register_namespace()` still resolves, and since registration is append-only + resolution is first-match, a cached FQCN can never go stale — no invalidation hook needed.

- **Single-writer Partition rotation reads the warm segment cache instead of force-scanning.** A `void_warranty()` (single-writer, no-peer) Partition — the Consumer's offsetlog, which rotates on every ~30s checkpoint with `OFFSETLOG_SEGMENT_SIZE=1` — was calling `scandir()` on every `do_rotate()` for peer-detection it can never need. `do_rotate()` now force-refreshes only for multi-writer partitions (`get_segments( ! $warranty_voided )`), and `get_segments()` treats a warranty-voided log's cache as never-stale (no peer can invalidate it, and every in-process modifier — rotate, cleanup, `truncate_after`, the size-sync, the scan path — keeps it in sync). Eliminates one `scandir` per checkpoint (and from `dump_metadata` poll reads, finally honouring its "no scandir on the poll path" promise). Multi-writer partitions are unchanged — they still force-refresh to detect a peer's rotation. A `Partition_Node::$scandir` test seam (lazily-defaulted to the real `scandir`) makes the no-rescan behaviour assertable; production is unaffected when it's null.

- **The shared chrome `ConnectionBanner` + `DevtoolsTabHost` now reskin under decorative themes.** Both `src/shared/` stylesheets used fixed `var(--np-*)` tokens, so they stayed Newspack-coloured under the console-selected skins. `ConnectionBanner.scss` now paints the universal `--oxide` error fill with `--paper` text — `--paper` is the surface colour, so it contrasts with `--oxide` on every skin (a fixed white would have vanished on bright-oxide skins like CRT's lime); `DevtoolsTabHost.scss`'s focus ring + active-tab underline use the universal `--cyan` accent. Under Newspack the tokens resolve to exactly the prior values (look identical), and literal fallbacks keep the prior look for a host without the token sheet. Consumers that inline these shared styles (`newspack-event-logger-nodes`) pick up the reskin on their next build.

- **De-god the Vault admin dashboard graph.** The single `vault:view` node that held the whole model (credential list + test results + loading/error + every verb's pending replies) is decomposed into two focused per-concern views, each behind its own receiver `Tee` so the debug overlay shows reply traffic per concern: `vault:list` (`VaultListViewNode`, fed by list/add/update/delete) and `vault:test` (`VaultTestViewNode`, per-server connection-probe results, correlated by server id). Built on the shared `SliceViewNode` base + its optional `PendingReplies` settle path; `VaultAdmin` reads each view via its own `useNodeState`. CRUD behavior unchanged; the old god node is removed.
- **De-god the Event Aggregator status dashboard.** The single `AggregatorViewNode` (fed by one `status` verb) that held the whole status model is decomposed into two genuine per-concern slices, each with its own slice verb, `SliceViewNode` subclass, and inspectable reply path. Server: `Aggregator_CI_Node` extracts the snapshot into a shared `build_snapshot()` and adds two read-only `slice_verb()` verbs — `summary` (`{ connected, total, server_now }`, connected rollup computed server-side) and `servers_status` (the snapshot as a sequential array); the legacy `status` verb is kept verbatim for the REST shim. Client: `useAggregatorStatusGraph` is rebuilt on `useBatchedPoll` + `addSliceFetcher` with two independent `Fetcher → receiver Tee → view` paths (`summary:view`, `servers:view`) batched into one POST per tick; `AggregatorStatus` reads each slice from its own view node. Behavior-preserving; the retired `AggregatorView` god node is removed.
- **The bundled example dashboard (`PublisherInsightsPage`) now mounts the `@newspack-nodes/debug-overlay`**, making its live per-slice node graph inspectable on the page (self-gated by `isDebugEnabled`). `docs/writing-a-dashboard.md` gains a "Make it inspectable: mount the debug overlay" section covering the mount, the `storageKey` naming convention, the gate, and that the overlay reads the live `mountExospine` graph (every node/edge/counter — the payoff of building the dashboard as a genuine graph).
- **A `Timer` with an interval > 1 s now ALWAYS hitchhikes the router TIMER and throttles in `fire_cb()` / `fireCb()`.** Instead of a dedicated event-framework / `setInterval` slot, a `>= 1000` ms interval registers on `_router` and fires only once `interval_ms` has elapsed since `last_fire_time` (`Core::$now` seconds; `interval_ms / 1000`); intervals `< 1 s` keep their own slot (the ~1 s router tick is too coarse for sub-second) and the no-interval hitchhike still fires every tick. Mirrored in the PHP (`class-timer-node.php`) and JS (`timer-node.js`) runtimes.
- **`TopicProbe_Node`, `HeartbeatNode`, and `UptimeNode` dropped their bespoke last-fire self-throttles** and now rely on the base Timer throttle via `set_timer( interval_ms )` (behavior unchanged); `MetadataNode` keeps its own gate because its `cd`-driven immediate re-poll mid-interval can't be expressed by the base throttle.
- **`useBatchedPoll` accepts an `intervalMs` option** that arms the owned poll Timer at that cadence (hitchhike + throttle, batching preserved) and re-arms when it changes — the seam the Performance Dashboard's refresh-rate selector drives.
- **`FetcherNode.command_args` may be a fire-time getter, and `addSliceFetcher` accepts an `argsFn` to set one — the minimal affordance for parameterized poll slices.** Until now a `Fetcher` (and therefore every `addSliceFetcher` slice) emitted a STATIC command-args string fixed at construction, so the batched-poll toolkit could only drive parameterless verbs (`counts`/`top`/`accumulated`). A poll dashboard whose verbs take live, UI-state-driven args (a perf URL list's `--sort`/`--order`/`--search`/`--offset`/`--server`, an overview's `--server`/`--breakdown`) had no way to track that state without re-wiring the graph each change. `FetcherNode.fill()` now resolves `command_args` at fire time: if it's a FUNCTION it CALLS it each tick to get the current args string (a non-string return coerces to `''`); a static string stays byte-identical to before (only opt-in callers pass a getter — every existing static-args test is unchanged and green). `addSliceFetcher` gains an optional `argsFn` that, when supplied, assigns the Fetcher's `command_args` to that getter; without it the Fetcher keeps the static (empty) args. This unblocks the Performance Dashboard's overview/urls poll slices (dashboard-restructure D1b) — the React hook gives each Fetcher a getter that reads the current filter/sort/page state, so each batched tick emits live args.
- **The hub's Worker Status / Topology Manager dashboard (`useTopologyManager`, driving Overview) is rebuilt as a genuine node graph on the `useBatchedPoll` + `addSliceFetcher` toolkit (plan D4).** The hook dropped the `useDashboardGraph` one-view-+-one-poll shortcut for `useBatchedPoll`, and now wires its two slices with `addSliceFetcher`: `topologymanager:timer → topologymanager:tee → { fetch-workers, fetch-topologies }`, each fanned to its own receiver Tee → view, so a tick's two commands batch into ONE HttpOut POST and each slice's reply has an independent pivot path. The 244-line `WorkerStatusTransformNode` enrich-join moves onto a graph EDGE via `addSliceFetcher`'s `transform` slot (the `workerstatus:in → workerstatus:view` edge) instead of being hand-wired as a separate `transform.target = view` hop. SERVER APPROACH: `dump_graph` stays ONE verb — its four sections (workers/consumers/logs/graph) must be joined from one coherent atomic snapshot (`reconstructWorkers`), so it can't be shattered into independently-timed slice verbs; it's fanned to one transform→view on the client. `topologies list` is genuinely independent → its own slice. (Neither needs a server change; the existing `Service_CI_Node::slice_verb()` builder is in place for CIs that genuinely do split.) The three mutations (`restart`/`activate`/`deactivate`) are now on-demand, graph-visible commands routed through `_shell/_http/<ci>` (so the debug overlay's `connect _shell` sees them) carrying an ID correlator that settles the matching reply on the view's `PendingReplies` — replacing the old hidden `_http`-only `interpreter.fill`. UI animation state stays out of the polling model: the `removingSegments` 400ms slide-out clear remains the `workerstatus:view` node's own UI concern, not a slice. The hook's return contract is unchanged (`{ topologies, supervisor, currentTime, readRate, writeRate, logPartitions, activate, deactivate, restart, connected }`), so `Overview.js` and its children render identically — the existing `useTopologyManager` jest suite passes as the behavior-preserving regression gate, plus new structural tests assert the genuine-graph wiring (toolkit boundary, transform-on-edge, one-batched-POST-per-tick).
- **`useBatchedPoll` gains an immediate first-paint poll on mount and a `paused` option.** The hook now fires ONE batched poll on mount (matching the old `useDashboardGraph`'s immediate-on-mount behavior — without it a dashboard waited a whole interval for its first data), gated on visible-AND-not-paused and bracketed by the same `http.lock()`/`http.flush()` so it's one POST; and a new `paused` opt stops the Timer's router-TIMER hitchhike (like a hidden tab) so a caller can suspend polling without unmounting (Overview passes `paused: dragging` to freeze the poll during a drag-reorder). Both benefit the example dashboard too (the example's render-only page test now flushes the mount poll under `act()`).
- **`example-ai-newsletter`: `usePublisherInsightsGraph` is rebuilt on the new `useBatchedPoll` + `addSliceFetcher` toolkit — the dashboard's proof, and the §4 of `docs/writing-a-dashboard.md` honesty seam closed.** The hook's ~50 lines of hand-wired `mountExospine` boilerplate (the `_shell` Tap, the `_http` HttpOut + injectable client, the fan-out Tee, the router-hitchhike Timer, the lock/flush batching bracket, and the page-visibility start/stop) and the per-slice `SLICES.forEach` make-Fetcher / receiver-Tee / view-node block both collapse into the two helpers; the hook is now `useBatchedPoll({ build: ({ interpreter, tee }) => SLICES.forEach( s => addSliceFetcher( interpreter, { ...s, tee, target: '_shell/_http/insights-demo' } ) ), … })` (175 lines → 76). Behavior is identical — the existing example jest suite (the one-router-TIMER-tick-batches-three-commands-into-ONE-POST test and the page-visibility test) passes unchanged as the regression gate. The guide's §4 now teaches `useBatchedPoll`/`addSliceFetcher` instead of the hand-wired wiring; its "← the next boilerplate to lift" sidebar becomes "← a substrate refinement", and the §9 recap table gains the two helper rows — the last hand-wired seam in the walkthrough, lifted into the substrate the moment a third caller copied it.
- **`example-ai-newsletter`: the `insights` god-verb on `Insights_CI_Demo_Node` is split into three slice verbs — `counts`, `top`, `accumulated`.** A god command is as bad as a god node: the one `insights` verb read the offsetlog snapshot and returned the whole `{sources, top, accumulated}` model. Now each verb returns ONE slice (`counts` → `{"sources":{…}}`, `top` → `{"top":[…]}` (top-10 by score), `accumulated` → `{"accumulated":N}`), so the dashboard fetches each independently — one `Fetcher` per verb, all batched into one POST per tick. The offsetlog read is extracted into a memoized per-request reader (`items()` calls `read_snapshot_items()` ONCE behind the new `$read_items` test seam, then caches the flattened items), so the three batched verbs share a single glob+unpack instead of reading thrice. Each verb still calls `require_manage_options()` (via the `Service_CI_Node` gate). `build_insights_json()` and the `insights` verb are removed; `read_insights_model()` stays for the end-to-end Pipeline test and is now built from the shared `read_snapshot_items()` + per-slice shapers (`shape_sources`/`shape_top`), never duplicating the glob/merge logic.
- **The `Consumer_Node` time-travel READ surface is consolidated into `dump_metadata`.** The three read-only request verbs `LIST_FRAMES`, `READ_STATE`, and `GET_OFFSET` are removed; their data now rides the existing canvas-poll payload via `Consumer_Node::dump_metadata()`, which the debugger UI already round-trips: `frames` is the offsetlog segment list `[{id,size}]` (one checkpoint = one segment = one keyframe; empty for ephemeral/no-offsetlog consumers) and `cursor` is the live source position `{seg,off}`. This is cheap — it reads only the warm `segments_cache` (no record reads, no `scandir` on the poll path). `SEEK_FRAME` accordingly changes from `<seg> <off>` to a single `<segment_id>` (the keyframe's offsetlog segment id from `frames[].id`): it reads that one offsetlog segment, restores the co-committed snapshot cache, and repositions the cursor to the record's source `{seg,off}`. The now-unused `list_frames()`/`read_state()`/`find_frame()`/`scan_offsetlog_entries()` methods and the `MAX_LISTED_FRAMES` constant are dropped. `GET_LAG` (and `PAUSE`/`PLAY`/`STEP`) are unchanged.
- **The topology-console Time Travel inspector panel reads from `dump_metadata` and drives the consumer's `:config` verbs through the existing invoke path** — no bespoke fetch/client. The inspector detects a consumer by the read surface it already holds (`node.frames` is an array AND `node.cursor` is present, threaded through `parseMetadata` from `dump_metadata()`), not a request verb. `TimeTravelPanel` renders a keyframe ruler (one marker per `node.frames` entry, ordered by id, the selected frame flagged current) plus a transport bar — rewind ⏮ / pause ⏸ / step ▌▶ / play ▶ / fast-forward ⏭ — where each button fires `onAction('invoke', nodeId, …)` as the consumer's `PAUSE` / `PLAY` / `STEP` / `SEEK_FRAME <segment_id>` `:config` commands. Frame selection is a **client-side model** that follows the live head by default — the newest frame is current and tracks live as new keyframes append. Rewind/FF PARK on a frame (`pinnedId`, walking the `node.frames` list prev/next, disabled at the ends — a paused keyframe scrub); PLAY un-parks (go live), as does a parked frame ageing out of the retained window. The live `cursor` ({seg,off}) is **informational only** and does NOT drive selection: a frame id is its offsetlog segment id (monotonic, climbs forever), an independent number space from the source-partition `cursor.seg`, so the two coincide only near zero. No state blob is rendered (`save_state` is a large nested object). The SLICE-2a bespoke request path is removed: `useConsumerFrames`, the `CommandClient.request()` / `buildRequestMessage()` additions, and both `unwrapRequestResponse` copies (`src/shared/utils` + `src/topology-console/utils`) are deleted along with the `LIST_FRAMES` / `READ_STATE` / `GET_OFFSET` references.
- **The Time Travel transport panel is now pause-gated with snap-to-keyframe rewind/fast-forward and a position readout.** PAUSE gates the whole bar: while following the head only ⏸ Pause is enabled (rewind / step / fast-forward / play are grayed); once paused, ⏸ disables and the rest enable subject to their own edge-disables. The `pinnedId` follow-head model is replaced by two pieces of client state — `parkedFrameId` (null = live/following-head; clamps back to null when the parked frame ages out of the retained window) and `steppedSincePark` (set by STEP, meaning the cursor now sits between keyframes). Rewind ⏮ snaps to keyframes: from live it lands on the NEWEST keyframe; after a STEP it snaps BACK to the current keyframe (not the one before); otherwise it walks to the previous keyframe (disabled on the oldest when not stepped). Fast-forward ⏭ walks to the next keyframe (disabled while live or on the newest). STEP keeps the panel paused and sets `steppedSincePark`; PLAY resumes following the head (un-parks, clears stepped). A new position line reports where the cursor sits ("live — after frame N", "on frame N", "between frame N and M", "after frame N", or "stepped past frame N"), and the current ruler marker carries a `--stepped` modifier when the cursor is between keyframes. The props contract (`frames`, `cursor`, `onTransport`) and the follow-head + clamp behavior are unchanged; verbs still fire as bare `onTransport('PAUSE'|'PLAY'|'STEP','')` and `onTransport('SEEK_FRAME', String(id))`.
- **The interactive `wp nodes cli` Dumper (`_output`) now sinks to the command interpreter.** A reply that lands on the cli's output node continues into the interpreter → router instead of terminating at the Dumper.
- **The hub's control buttons now follow the same stock-WP-under-Newspack / themed-under-decorative rule as the rest.** The Overview "+ New Topology", "Fold all" / "Unfold all", per-row "Edit" and "Restart" (↻), the Vault "+ Add Server", and the Raw Logs Pause/Clear buttons were custom-classed `<button>`s (never WP-stock); they now carry the WP `.button` (/`button-small`) classes in markup, and their bespoke `secondary-button`/`dark-button` SCSS visuals are dropped (layout kept) so WP core styles them under Newspack and the shared `.topology-app:not(.theme-newspack)…` rule themes them under decorative skins. (The Restart ↻ keeps its amber `--brass` icon cue under Newspack.)
- **Hub buttons are stock WP under the Newspack/Newspack-Brand themes and themed under the decorative themes.** One shared `devtools-hub.scss` ruleset — scoped to `.newspack-nodes-theme:not(.theme-newspack):not(.theme-newspack-brand)` and drawn from the universal theme tokens (`--cyan`/`--paper`/`--ink-3`/`--oxide`/…) — replaces the Vault tab's per-surface `.button` re-skins. Under the two Newspack skins the selector doesn't match, so buttons fall through to stock WP core-ui; under every decorative theme they take that theme's colors. Defined once for the whole hub instead of per tab.
- **The Event Aggregator hub tab reads the universal theme tokens, so it re-skins under every theme** (identical under Newspack). Its `base.scss` token layer and `aggregator-status.scss` read `--paper`/`--ink`/`--cyan`/`--sage`/`--brass`/`--oxide` and the new `--*-subtle` tints instead of the Newspack-only `--np-*` colors.
- **The Event Dashboards hub tab (overview, topology rows, worker status, summary cards, raw logs) reads the universal theme tokens, so it re-skins under every theme.** Its `base.scss` token layer and the per-surface SCSS read `--paper`/`--ink`/`--cyan`/`--sage`/`--brass`/`--oxide` + the `--*-subtle` tints; the summary-card chart accents use the new `--chart-*` tokens. The intentionally-dark `$term-*` log-surface literals are unchanged.
- **The debug overlay's status accents read the universal theme tokens** (`--brass`/`--oxide`/`--paper-2`), so its warning/error markers re-skin with the active theme; the existing hex fallbacks are kept.
- **Topic chart series colors re-skin with the active hub theme.** `TopicsChart` resolves the theme's `--chart-1..8` tokens at render time (via `getComputedStyle` off the themed `.topology-app` root) and re-resolves on theme change — a new `useThemeToken` hook tracks the live skin through the `storage` event and a `MutationObserver` on the themed ancestor's class. The shared 20-color `PALETTE` remains the fallback when the tokens are absent.
- **The Vault tab surfaces are driven from the universal theme tokens, so the whole tab re-skins under every theme** (identical under Newspack, which aliases the universal tokens to its `--np-*`). Its table/header/row/modal styling reads `--paper`/`--paper-2`/`--paper-shadow`/`--ink`/`--ink-3` instead of the Newspack-only `--np-*` color tokens; the structural `--np-radius-md` is unchanged.
- **The per-field config `overlay` opt-out is removed; every setting now overlays the config file uniformly.** `Config_System\Field` no longer takes an `overlay` flag and no longer exposes `is_overlaid()` — `Schema::overlay_keys()` returns every field with a non-empty key (every settable option is an overlay key). The substrate's three `remote_*` settings (`remote_num_segments`/`remote_segment_size`/`remote_max_lifespan`) are no longer special-cased as direct-read: they overlay into `Config::load_config()` like every other setting, so a stored `remote_*` resolves through the overlay and an unset one carries the config-file default. `Settings_Renderer`'s Effective/Override columns are now uniform across all fields (no `overlay`-flag branch). `Options_Overlay::apply()` and `Config::load_config()` are unchanged — they simply receive the now-complete key list.
- **The "Effective Configuration" panel now lives in the shared `Config_System\Settings_Renderer`** as `effective_config_rows( Schema, prefix, effective )` + `render_effective_config_section( Schema, prefix, effective )` (plus the restart-impact and value-formatting helpers), so both `newspack-nodes` and `newspack-event-logger-nodes` render the panel from one implementation instead of each carrying its own copy. The substrate `Admin::render_effective_config_section()` is now a thin delegate; the per-row data shape is exercised against the shared renderer directly. The Effective column reports the overlay-resolved `Config::load_config()` value for every field — an unset setting shows its file default, uniform across all fields instead of a blank cell.

### Fixed

- **Dashboard stylesheets cache-bust on their own content hash.** `Admin::enqueue_react_page()` enqueued `index.css` with the JS bundle's `index.asset.php` version, so a SCSS-only rebuild (JS hash unchanged) left the stylesheet behind a stale `?ver=` — a CSS-only change needed a hard-refresh to land. It now versions the stylesheet by `md5_file(index.css)`, independent of the script bundle — centralized in the reusable `Admin::css_cache_version()` helper, which the sibling plugins (event-logger-nodes, pyrobase, nuclear-gyrobase) route their dashboard/admin stylesheets through too.
